## 2026-05-08 - US-0011
- **Implemented**: Security and dependency verification gates. Layered the
  vulnerability scan, lint suite, and dependency-review action on top of the
  existing commit gate; added a single local entry point (`scripts/verify.sh`)
  that mirrors the CI pipeline; documented the minimum required checks for
  commit and release in `SECURITY.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`; added an
  end-to-end secret-leak regression net that drives the production
  exit-code path with a sentinel token across every redaction-relevant
  rendering path.
- **Files changed**:
  - `scripts/verify.sh` (new) — required + optional checks, `--release`,
    `--strict`, `--quiet` flags. Reports missing optional tools explicitly
    rather than silently skipping.
  - `.golangci.yml` (new) — configured linter set: `govet`, `staticcheck`,
    `errcheck`, `ineffassign`, `unused`, `bodyclose`, `gosec` (G304
    excluded), `errorlint`, `gofmt`, `goimports`, `misspell`, `unconvert`,
    `revive`. Test files relax cosmetic linters; `internal/api/data/`
    relaxes verbosity linters for verbatim payloads.
  - `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — added a `security` job that runs
    `govulncheck`, `staticcheck`, and `golangci-lint` on every push and
    PR. Existing test/goreleaser jobs unchanged.
  - `.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml` (new) —
    `actions/dependency-review-action@v4` on every PR with
    `fail-on-severity: high` and an explicit OSI license allowlist.
  - `SECURITY.md` (new) — vulnerability disclosure process, threat model,
    redaction contract, required verification gates table, dependency
    review pointer, and a best-effort disclosure timeline.
  - `CONTRIBUTING.md` (new) — minimum required checks before commit,
    minimum required checks before release, optional-tool install hints,
    coding conventions, dependency-review checklist, and a Ralph Loop
    pointer.
  - `README.md` — added Security and Contributing sections linking the
    new docs.
  - `internal/cli/redaction_security_test.go` (new) — the canonical
    end-to-end secret-leak regression net.
  - `ralph/prd.json` — `US-0011.passes` flipped to `true`.
- **Verification run**:
  - `gofmt -w .` — clean.
  - `go mod tidy` — clean.
  - `go vet ./...` — clean.
  - `go test ./...` — all pass (cli 1.106s, race 2.656s, total all green).
  - `go test -race ./...` — all pass.
  - `bash scripts/verify.sh --quiet` — exit 0; reports the four optional
    tools as missing (govulncheck, staticcheck, golangci-lint, goreleaser)
    rather than silently skipping.
  - `govulncheck ./...` — installed and ran locally; surfaced two
    pre-existing stdlib advisories tied to the host toolchain
    (`go1.26.2` vs fixed `go1.26.3`). See "Remaining risks" below — the
    point of US-0011 was to wire the gate, not to bump the toolchain.
- **Results**: All required checks pass. The new secret-leak suite has 6
  top-level test cases (some table-driven with sub-cases) — every one
  passes. The lint and vulnerability gates are live in CI starting with
  the next push.
- **Remaining risks / follow-ups**:
  - The local `govulncheck` run found two stdlib vulns (`GO-2026-4971`,
    `GO-2026-4918`) reported against `net@go1.26.2` (fixed in
    `net@go1.26.3`). These exist on the developer host's toolchain. CI
    installs Go via `setup-go` with `go-version-file: go.mod` (currently
    `go 1.24`), which should pick up the latest 1.24.x patch — fixes for
    both advisories are typically backported, but the CI run will be the
    authoritative answer. If CI flags the same advisories, the
    follow-up is to add a `toolchain` directive in `go.mod` pinning a
    patched version (e.g. `toolchain go1.26.3`) or bump the `go`
    directive to a known-good patch. This is **not** a US-0011 scope
    item — US-0011 is the wiring; the toolchain bump is a separate,
    isolated change.
  - `staticcheck` and `golangci-lint` were not run locally (not
    installed). CI will be the first place they execute. If either flags
    a finding in the existing codebase the immediate follow-up is to
    fix it; the lint config is intentionally strict because the security
    gate is part of the public contract.
- **Learnings for future iterations**:
  - **Patterns discovered**:
    - The CI gate has two natural tiers: the `test` job (correctness;
      runs on every push) and the `security` job (vulns + lint;
      independent so a slow vulnerability database fetch does not gate
      the test signal). `goreleaser-check` already lived in its own job
      for the same reason. Future gates (e.g. SBOM generation) should
      follow the same pattern.
    - Secret-leak tests are most effective when they exercise the
      *renderer* (Renderer.Error, Renderer.Logf, Renderer.Data) through
      the production exit-code path rather than constructing a
      Renderer in isolation. The integration suite catches missing
      wire-ups (e.g. a new command that bypassed `r.Logf`) that
      renderer-only unit tests would not.
    - GitHub Actions writes a workflow-injection warning whenever a
      run-step uses `${{ github.event.* }}` interpolation. Keep
      vulnerable inputs out of `run:` blocks — use `env:` indirection.
      None of the new workflow files use untrusted inputs in `run:`.
  - **Gotchas encountered**:
    - `actions/dependency-review-action@v4` only runs on `pull_request`
      events; pushing directly to a branch will not trigger it. That is
      intentional (the action diffs base-against-head) but worth
      documenting so contributors don't expect it from a push.
    - `golangci-lint` v2 requires a `version: 2` field in the config
      file; v1 does not accept it. The `.golangci.yml` here targets
      v1's grammar (no top-level `version:`); golangci-lint-action
      installs the latest stable, which currently still resolves to
      v1's compatible mode. If CI fails on schema, pin the action to a
      v1 release.
    - `gosec` flags G304 ("file inclusion via variable") on every
      `os.Open` taking a CLI-supplied path. That is the entire point of
      `--input <path>` and `--config <path>`; we explicitly exclude
      G304 in `.golangci.yml` and rely on path validation done in the
      command layer instead.
  - **Useful context**:
    - The redactor is defence-in-depth: classification of errors and
      explicit field handling are still primary. The new test file is
      a regression net, not the security boundary itself.
    - `verify.sh`'s "report, never silently skip" rule is a project
      principle, not a tooling quirk. The Ralph Loop iteration pattern
      depends on every gap being visible in `progress.txt` so future
      iterations can act on it.

    `runManifest` accept a `*curated.Registry`; added
    `curatedDomainNames` and `collectCuratedCommands` projection
    helpers; updated the human-mode banner to surface curated counts.
  - `internal/cli/manifest_cmd_test.go` — new tests:
    `TestManifest_JSONListsCuratedDomains`,
    `TestManifest_JSONIncludesCuratedCommands` (checks the JSON wire
    shape directly so a missing field cannot be hidden by struct
    decoding), `TestManifest_RendersCuratedCommandPayload` (end-to-end
    projection with a custom registry, including the defensive-copy
    invariant), `TestManifest_DefaultCuratedRegistryMatchesAPISpec`
    (live spec regression mirror).
  - `internal/cli/AGENTS.md` — new bullet documenting the curated →
    manifest contract and the "never replace raw API coverage" rule.
  - `docs/curated-commands.md` (new) — the human-facing policy
    document. Covers domains, naming rules, recommended verb sets per
    domain, the manifest contract (with sample JSON), and the
    step-by-step add-a-curated-command workflow.
  - `ralph/prd.json` — set US-0012 `passes: true`.
- **Verification run**:
  - `gofmt -w .` — clean.
  - `go mod tidy` — clean.
  - `go vet ./...` — clean.
  - `go test ./...` — all packages pass (curated package included).
  - `go test -race ./...` — all packages pass.
  - `bash scripts/verify.sh --quiet` — full local gate clean; optional
    tools (`govulncheck`, `staticcheck`, `golangci-lint`, `goreleaser`)
    reported as not installed exactly as the project policy requires.
  - Smoke: `go run ./cmd/yalla --json manifest | jq '.data |
    {curated_domains, curated_commands}'` returns the canonical
    seven-domain list and an empty `curated_commands` array.
- **Tools NOT available locally** (per project policy): `goimports`,
  `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`, `govulncheck`, `goreleaser`. Same
  status as previous iterations; documented here so the gap stays
  visible.
- **Remaining risks / follow-ups**:
  - The `defaultCommands` slice is empty by design — every subsequent
    curated-command story (US-001x onward) MUST append its descriptor
    there, with a non-empty `OperationIDs` list, before wiring the
    Cobra command. The manifest, docs, and validation plumbing pick
    them up automatically.
  - The Cobra-command Examples for any curated command should mirror
    `Command.HumanExample` / `Command.JSONExample` so the manifest,
    `--help`, and `docs/curated-commands.md` stay in sync. A future
    helper that returns a Cobra-style `Example` block from a
    `curated.Command` would centralise that, but is out of scope
    for the foundation story.
- **Learnings for future iterations**:
  - Foundation stories pay off when they bake in the contract test:
    `TestDefaultRegistry_VerifiesAgainstSpec` (and its manifest mirror)
    means a stale operationId fails CI before the binary ships.
    Without it, curated commands could drift from the OpenAPI spec
    silently.
  - Decoding the manifest into a `map[string]json.RawMessage` (rather
    than the typed struct) is the cleanest way to assert "this JSON
    field exists on the wire". The struct decoder cheerfully
    zero-fills missing fields, hiding regressions.
  - Defensive-copy assertions belong on every projection that returns
    a slice ("mutate the projected slice, re-read from the source,
    expect no bleed"). Catching a shared backing array in test is much
    cheaper than chasing the eventual consistency bug.
  - Banning short aliases via a hint-bearing map (`{"ls": "list"}`)
    gives validation errors that tell the developer the right answer
    instead of just rejecting the wrong one. Worth replicating any
    time the policy is "thou shalt not X" and there is a canonical Y.
  - The `OperationLookup` interface kept the curated tests free of the
    OpenAPI embed dance. The same pattern (a tiny adapter interface)
    would help any future cross-package contract test.

## 2026-05-08 - API-0001
- **Implemented**: First per-operation API coverage story
  (admin-setupMonitoring, POST /admin.setupMonitoring, tag admin) plus
  the scalable, append-only contract-test harness every subsequent
  API-XXXX story will reuse.
- **Files changed**:
  - `internal/cli/api_coverage_test.go` (new) — defines
    `apiCoverageCase` (the per-story input record) and
    `coveredAPIOperations` (the append-only slice). Five
    table-driven tests run the same assertions per case:
    `TestAPICoverage_RegistryInvariants` (id/method/path/tag match
    `api.Default()`), `TestAPICoverage_SchemaCommandWorks`
    (`yalla schema get --json` envelope), `TestAPICoverage_ManifestListsOperation`
    (operation id is in `yalla manifest --json` operations.ids),
    `TestAPICoverage_SuccessRoundTrip` (httptest server validates
    method, path, Authorization header, content-type, body, and the
    success envelope shape), and `TestAPICoverage_RepresentativeFailure`
    (default 401 → CodeAuth, configurable per case). Fixture body for
    admin-setupMonitoring mirrors the openapi.json schema's required
    shape (`metricsConfig` with `server.refreshRate` + `containers`).
  - `internal/cli/AGENTS.md` — new "Per-operation API coverage"
    section documenting the harness contract for future API-XXXX
    contributors (sorted-by-story-id, override FailureStatus/Code
    when 401 is not the right representative failure, SampleBody
    must mirror the OpenAPI required shape verbatim).
  - `ralph/prd.json` — flipped `API-0001.passes` to `true`.
- **Verification run**:
  - `gofmt -w .` — clean (one auto-format pass on the new test file).
  - `go vet ./...` — clean.
  - `go mod tidy` — no changes.
  - `go test ./...` — all packages pass; the five new
    `TestAPICoverage_*` subtests under `API-0001/admin-setupMonitoring`
    PASS.
  - `go test -race ./...` — clean.
  - `bash scripts/verify.sh --quiet` — full local gate clean. The
    same four optional tools as in earlier stories
    (`govulncheck`, `staticcheck`, `golangci-lint`, `goreleaser`)
    are still not installed locally and are documented in the
    verify.sh banner; this matches the project's "report, never
    silently skip" policy.
- **Remaining risks / follow-ups**:
  - The harness defaults the failure leg to 401→CodeAuth. A handful
    of upcoming operations (rate-limit-prone create/delete, conflict-
    prone update) will want to override `FailureStatus` /
    `FailureCode` to assert the more representative path; document
    that as a checklist item when we get to those PRD entries.
  - Body fixtures are currently free-form JSON. We do **not**
    validate the fixture against the OpenAPI request schema today;
    if a fixture drifts from the schema, only the wire-side equality
    check protects us. A future enhancement (post-coverage) is to
    pipe each `SampleBody` through a schema validator using the
    embedded JSON schema fragments — out of scope for this story.
- **Learnings for future iterations**:
  - **One harness for ~440 stories**: hand-rolling a separate test
    file per API-XXXX story would mean ~440 near-identical files and
    the same number of code-review rituals. The data-driven slice
    keeps the per-story diff to a single struct literal while still
    giving each story a named subtest path
    (`TestAPICoverage_*/API-XXXX/<operationId>`) so a regression
    points back to its PRD entry without grep gymnastics.
  - **Use `setupAPICallServer` from the existing test suite**: the
    helper wires an httptest server to `YALLA_BASE_URL` and seeds
    `YALLA_TOKEN` via `t.Setenv`, which means our coverage tests
    cannot run with `t.Parallel()` — same constraint as every other
    env-mutating test in `internal/cli`.
  - **Body equality through JSON normalize**: comparing wire bytes
    directly fails on whitespace differences (the CLI re-serialises
    JSON through json.Decoder which collapses pretty-printed
    fixtures). Round-tripping both sides through `json.Unmarshal` +
    `json.Marshal` before comparison eliminates the flake without
    losing structural fidelity.
  - **Per-operation registry assertion is intentionally redundant**:
    `internal/api/registry_test.go` already locks the full operation
    set; per-story checks duplicate that for a precise reason — when
    an assertion fails, the failing subtest name names the PRD entry
    so the contributor knows which story to revisit instead of
    decoding which row in a 446-element slice broke.

    (INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR), but those broader status-mapping invariants
    are already exercised cross-cuttingly by `internal/api/client_test.go`.

    schema. With API-0014 introducing the first `anyOf` field in the

    `GET`, path `/application.search`, tag `application`, no body.
    `SampleQuery` populates a representative subset (`q`, `owner`,
    `limit`, `offset`) of the spec's 11 all-optional parameters; numeric
    values (`limit`/`offset`) travel as decimal strings to match the
    untyped wire grammar of HTTP query strings. `SuccessResponse: "{}"`
    mirrors the spec's `additionalProperties:false` empty 200 body.
  - `ralph/prd.json` — set API-0035 `passes: true`.
- **Verification run**:
  - `gofmt -w .` — clean.
  - `go mod tidy` — clean.
  - `go vet ./...` — clean.
  - `go test ./...` — `ok github.com/JuribaDev/yalla/internal/cli` (full
    coverage harness incl. registry/schema/manifest/success/failure
    legs).
  - `go test -race ./...` — clean.
- **Tools NOT available locally** (per the verification policy):
  `goimports`, `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`, `govulncheck`, `goreleaser`.
- **Remaining risks / follow-ups**:
  - The fixture only exercises 4 of 11 query parameters. That is
    intentional (representative coverage of free-text + scoped filter +
    numeric pagination) but a future schema-validator wiring may want
    to extend the case to all 11 to lock the full param surface.
  - `application-search` is the FIRST application/* coverage entry with
    fully-optional query params. If a future Dokploy revision tightens
    `required: true` on any of these fields, the registry-invariant
    test will still pass but agents would silently get 4xx — only the
    spec digest pinning (`sourceApi.sha256` in `ralph/prd.json` and
    `EmbeddedSpecSHA256`) catches that drift.
- **Learnings for future iterations**:
  - All-optional query parameters are wire-valid empty: the harness
    handles a fully-empty `SampleQuery` (see API-0006 `ai-getAll`) but
    when params *do* exist the verbatim-comparator at
    `runAPICoverageSuccess` insists they survive the
    `--input.query` → request-URL round-trip exactly, including
    multi-valued slices and ordering.
  - Numeric-typed query params (`limit`/`offset`, both spec-typed as
    `number`) are sent over the wire as their decimal-string form
    inside `--input`'s `query: map[string][]string`. There is no
    separate "numeric" query input shape; HTTP query strings are
    untyped.
  - When extending the coverage table with a new entry, prefer to
    populate a *representative* subset of optional fields (free-text +
    scoped + numeric) rather than the full surface. The
    success-leg comparator is precise about whatever you put in; the
    bigger the fixture, the larger the diff blast-radius if Dokploy
    renames a param. Subset coverage hits the contract bits that
    matter (verbatim CLI propagation + numeric grammar) without
    over-specifying.

  minimal-but-valid fixture is therefore `{"applicationId": "..."}`,
  staying robust if a future schema validator is wired into the harness.
  200 response is `{}` with `additionalProperties: false`, matching
  every other application/* mutation peer.
- **Verification run**:
  - `gofmt -w .` — clean.
  - `go mod tidy` — clean.
  - `go vet ./...` — clean.
  - `go test ./...` — all packages `ok`; `internal/cli` runtime 1.137s.
  - `go test -race ./...` — all packages `ok`; `internal/cli` runtime
    2.431s with the race detector on.
- **Tools NOT available locally** (unchanged from prior stories):
  `goimports`, `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`, `govulncheck`,
  `goreleaser`.
- **Remaining risks / follow-ups**: none. The harness covers registry
  invariants, schema reachability, manifest inclusion, success
  round-trip, and the representative failure path from the same single
  entry.
- **Learnings for future iterations**:
  - The Dokploy `application-update` schema is the largest in the
    `application` tag (90+ optional properties spanning app metadata,
    swarm config, every supported git provider, build args, registry
    IDs, preview deployment toggles, and resource limits). The required
    set is still just `applicationId`, so the minimal-applicationId
    POST family fixture (used by start/stop/reload/redeploy/delete) is
    the right baseline — adding optional fields would only matter once
    the harness gains a JSON-Schema validator. Until then, less is
    more.
  - When a schema's `additionalProperties` is *unset* (vs `false`),
    JSON Schema treats it as permissive. `application-update` request
    body falls into that bucket, so a future validator would not
    reject extra keys; do not over-tighten the fixture for that
    reason alone.

## 2026-05-08 - API-0039

  `application-updateTraefikConfig` (POST `/application.updateTraefikConfig`)
  via the shared `apiCoverageCase` harness.

  - `internal/cli/api_coverage_test.go` — appended a single
    `apiCoverageCase` for API-0039. Unlike the broader minimal-applicationId
    POST family, the OpenAPI schema requires *both* `applicationId` and
    `traefikConfig` strings (no optional siblings), so the minimal-but-valid
    fixture carries both. `traefikConfig` is a literal YAML snippet (with
    embedded newlines + colon) so the success leg exercises real JSON
    serialisation of an embedded raw-text payload through `yalla api call`.

    mutation peer.

- **Tools NOT available locally** (unchanged): `goimports`, `golangci-lint`,
  `staticcheck`, `govulncheck`, `goreleaser`.
- **Remaining risks / follow-ups**:
  - The fixture's `traefikConfig` value is syntactically YAML but the
    Dokploy server is not exercised against a real Traefik validator in
    the test (httptest server returns `{}` for any request). A future
    contract-test layer that round-trips a known-bad Traefik string
    against a stricter mock would catch validation regressions; out of
    scope for raw API coverage stories.
- **Learnings for future iterations**:
  - When a request schema requires multiple top-level strings (not just
    `applicationId`), keep the fixture minimal-but-valid by including
    every required field. The harness forwards bytes verbatim, so an
    incomplete body would still pass the success leg today (the httptest
    server doesn't validate) but would mask schema drift if Dokploy ever
    tightened its server-side validator.
  - Embedding newlines and colons inside a JSON string field is a useful
    smoke test for the encoder path — the harness sends bytes verbatim,
    but a future validator hook would reject improperly escaped values.

  - Targeted: `go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestAPICoverage' -v -count=1`
    confirms all 5 sub-phases (RegistryInvariants, SchemaCommandWorks,
    ManifestListsOperation, SuccessRoundTrip, RepresentativeFailure) fire and
    PASS for `API-0089/compose-search`.
- Remaining risks / follow-ups: none specific to this story. Future
  compose/* GET stories with all-optional query params (none currently
  pending in the priority-2 queue) can copy this fixture verbatim and just
  rotate the slug.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - When adding a new structural-first fixture (e.g. all-optional query
    params for the first time on a tag), point the comment at the closest
    cross-tag precedent (API-0035 here) — that's the canonical way the
    roster signals "this pattern already exists, just on a different tag".
  - HTTP query strings are untyped on the wire, so OpenAPI `number` query
    params travel through the `--input` JSON `query` field as strings.
    Use canonical decimal grammar (`"10"` / `"0"`, never `"10.0"`) so a
    future schema validator that re-coerces query strings to numbers
    still accepts them — same convention API-0035 established.
  - Don't bloat fixtures into N-key maps when N is large. Pick a
    representative slice (free-text + scoped + numeric pagination = 3
    facets) so the success-leg `r.URL.Query()` re-read still proves
    end-to-end forwarding without making the diff a wall of slugs.
  - The harness's five-phase contract (`TestAPICoverage_*`) ranges over
    `coveredAPIOperations`, so adding a single struct literal is the entire
    surface area of a coverage story — never touch the harness functions
    themselves unless the contract is changing for ALL stories.

  than this list endpoint; story-specific FailureStatus/FailureCode
  overrides are reserved for entries where 404 is the canonical
  miss (id-shaped lookups).

  organization/*: `*-active` (singular, principal-scoped) vs.
  `*-all` (plural, membership-scoped). This is analogous to the
  cross-tag pair API-0098 (`deployment-allCentralized`) and

    manifest inclusion, httptest success, representative-failure leg) for
    a `single-required-scalar` POST — appending one struct literal
    completes the story without any new test plumbing.
  - `organization-removeInvitation` notably **omits** the 404 response code
    that the lookup-shape GET `organization-one` declares — Dokploy's tRPC
    surface collapses missing-invitation into a 400 (validation) rather
    than a 404 (not found). The harness default 401→CodeAuth failure leg
    is the right call; do not invent a per-case 404 representative-failure
    variant for delete-by-id mutations in this tag.
  - Per-case fixture token convention reaffirmed:
    `<tag>-cov-<slug>-<storyID>` → `yalla-coverage-org-removeInvitation-0252`
    keeps `git grep` traceable without colliding with API-0249/0250
    fixtures (`yalla-coverage-org-create-0249`,
    `yalla-coverage-org-delete-0250`).

## 2026-05-08 - API-0293
- Added apiCoverageCase entry for `project-duplicate`
  (POST /project.duplicate, tag `project`) to
  `internal/cli/api_coverage_test.go`, sorted immediately after
  API-0292. This is the second mutation peer in the project/*
  roster and the first project/* entry to exercise a nested
  array-of-objects body shape.
- Spec-derived body shape (verified against
  `internal/api/data/openapi.json > /project.duplicate > post`):
  required scalars `sourceEnvironmentId` + `name`; optional plain
  string `description`; optional booleans `includeServices`
  (default `true`) and `duplicateInSameProject` (default `false`);
  optional array-of-objects `selectedServices` with each element
  carrying required `id` (string) and required `type` enum
  (application|postgres|mariadb|mongo|mysql|redis|compose). Per
  the API-0010 / API-0014 / API-0249 / API-0292 every-optional-
  populated convention all four optionals are populated. Booleans
  are flipped to the *inverse* of their spec defaults so the
  success-leg byte forwarding actually transmits the chosen
  value rather than coinciding with what a server-side default
  would emit. `selectedServices` carries one element with
  `type: "application"` enum-pinned (per the API-0255 enum-
  constrained-scalar rule). Per-case fixture token base
  `proj-cov-duplicate-0293`; nested element id
  `app-cov-duplicate-0293-svc1`; both are unique across the
  project/* roster and never collide with `org-cov-*`.
- Files changed:
  - `internal/cli/api_coverage_test.go` (new struct literal,
    +118 lines including comment header)
  - `ralph/prd.json` (passes flag flipped to true for API-0293)
  - `ralph/progress.txt` (this entry)
- Verification (repo root):
  - `gofmt -w .` — clean
  - `go mod tidy` — no changes
  - `go vet ./...` — clean
  - `go test ./... -count=1` — all packages OK
  - `go test -race ./... -count=1` — all packages OK
  - `goimports`, `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`, `govulncheck`,
    and `goreleaser` not installed locally; documented in earlier
    entries as the verification-tools baseline gap.
- Results: harness loop now runs the five contract checks
  (registry / schema / manifest / success round-trip /
  representative failure) for API-0293 alongside the prior 102
  covered operations. No source files outside the
  `apiCoverageCase` table needed editing — the operation
  registry, schema generator, and manifest renderer are spec-
  driven from `internal/api/data/openapi.json`.
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - API-0294 `project-one` is the next entry in the project/*
    arc and per the API-0290 / API-0291 / API-0292 reservation
    is the legitimate home for the project/* tag's first
    filter-shaped GET. It will be the first project/* peer to
    populate `SampleQuery` (the spec declares a required
    `projectId` query parameter and no body), and the first
    appropriate place in the project/* roster to lift the
    harness default failure leg from 401 → CodeAuth to
    404 → CodeNotFound — auth (401) has been re-proven across
    every project/* peer so far, and 404 is precisely the
    failure shape a single-resource lookup must surface.
  - API-0295 `project-remove`, API-0297 `project-update` are
    expected to share the project-duplicate `{required, +optional}`
    pattern but with simpler bodies (likely
    `{projectId}` for remove and `{projectId, name?, description?}`
    for update). They can copy this entry's slug-namespace
    discipline but must rederive their `SampleBody` literal from
    the spec — the array-of-objects shape used here is
    project-duplicate-specific and does not transfer.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - For mutation peers with optional booleans that have non-
    `false` spec defaults, **flip the fixture value to the
    inverse of the default** (`includeServices: true` (default)
    → `false` (fixture); `duplicateInSameProject: false`
    (default) → `true` (fixture)). This keeps the success-leg
    body forwarding invariant observable end-to-end: a server
    rendering server-side defaults would round-trip the same
    bytes regardless of CLI behaviour, but inverted booleans
    force the wire to actually carry the chosen value through
    the CLI → API client → httptest server path. The
    every-optional-populated convention is therefore really
    every-optional-populated-with-non-default-where-feasible.
  - Nested array-of-objects body fixtures pre-exist in the ai/*
    roster (API-0004 `ai-deploy` with `domains[]` and
    `configFiles[]`) — when adding the first such fixture in a
    new tag arc, grep for the prior tag's array-of-objects entry
    to inherit the indentation style (`[` / `\n\t\t\t\t{` /
    `\n\t\t\t}` / `\n\t\t]`) rather than re-deriving it.
  - Enum-constrained array element fields follow the same rule
    as scalar enums established at API-0255 `organization-
    updateMemberRole`: pin to **one** fixed enum value and do not
    duplicate alternates across additional array elements. The
    schema-validator coverage for the alternate enum branches is
    handled at the spec-level by the registry, not at the per-
    operation success-leg fixture.
  - `description` in the project/* tag is not uniformly nullable:
    API-0292 `project-create` declared `anyOf [string, null]`,
    while API-0293 `project-duplicate` declares plain `string`.
    Always cross-check the per-operation spec for nullability —
    the every-optional-populated rule's "populate the string
    branch" guidance from API-0292 still works for both cases
    (the populated string is valid in either schema), but
    schema-level assertions about which branch is exercised
    differ between the two peers.

## 2026-05-08 - API-0340
- What was implemented: Coverage for `server-getServerMetrics` (GET

  parameters `url` / `token` / `dataPoints`, all string per the spec).
  Added a single `apiCoverageCase` struct literal to

  invariants, schema reachability, manifest inclusion, the
  httptest-backed success exchange (per-key `r.URL.Query()`
  re-assertion), and the default 401 → CodeAuth failure leg from
  that single literal.
- Files changed:
  * `internal/cli/api_coverage_test.go` (new struct literal)
  * `ralph/prd.json` (flipped `API-0340.passes` to `true`)
  * `ralph/progress.txt` (this entry)
- Verification run:
  * `gofmt -w .` → clean
  * `goimports` → not installed (consistent with prior iterations)
  * `go mod tidy` → no changes
  * `go vet ./...` → exit 0
  * `go test ./...` → all 9 packages PASS
  * `go test -race ./...` → all 9 packages PASS
  * `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`, `govulncheck`, `goreleaser` →
    not installed (documented in prior progress entries; no change
    this iteration)
- Results: 114/462 PRD stories now passing; CI-equivalent local
  checks all green.
- Remaining risks or follow-ups: None specific to this story. The
  multi-query-param shape is now first-classed in the coverage
  harness; future `*-getServerMetrics`-style peers in other tags
  and any other multi-required-query GET should mirror this entry.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **API-0340 was the FIRST multi-key SampleQuery case in the
    entire coverage roster.** I ran a regex sweep before adding
    the entry — every prior `SampleQuery` block (24 cases across
    ai/*, organization/*, project/*, and the API-0339
    `server-getDefaultCommand` opener) declared exactly one key.
    The harness already supports multi-key maps natively
    (`for k, want := range tc.SampleQuery { … seenQuery[k] … }`)
    so no harness change was needed — but document the milestone
    in the case comment so future grep-driven discovery works.
  - **Per-key fixture token slug pattern.** When a single case
    has multiple secrets/values, prefix every value with the
    same `<tag>-cov-<slug>-<storyID>` base so a leaked value is
    traceable to one story. I used:
      * `url`        → `https://srv-cov-getServerMetrics-0340.example.test`
      * `token`      → `srv-cov-getServerMetrics-0340-token`
      * `dataPoints` → `50`
    The `.example.test` reserved domain (RFC 2606) means even an
    accidental real-world fetch can never escape the test sandbox.
  - **`token` query param is NOT a Dokploy auth credential.** It
    is a *target-server* token that Dokploy forwards downstream to
    a remote agent host — orthogonal to the redaction security
    suite's bearer-token sentinel checks. Picking a fixture-shaped
    value (no `Bearer` prefix, no base64-looking entropy) keeps
    the security suite clean. The success envelope's `URL` field
    will be redacted by `output.RedactURL` per the existing
    `redaction_security_test.go::?token=` test, but the harness
    does not assert on the `URL` field — only on
    `OperationID`/`Method`/`Status`/`SchemaVersion` — so no
    interaction.
  - **`schemaType: string` for numeric values.** The spec declares
    `dataPoints` as `string` even though it is conceptually a
    count; the `--input` JSON's `query` field is `map[string][]string`,
    so the value goes in as `"50"` not `50`. Mirroring the spec
    type verbatim is the safe default for any future query param
    that "looks numeric but is declared string".

## 2026-05-08 - API-0342
- What was implemented: Coverage for `server-one` (GET /server.one,
  tag `server`, single required query parameter `serverId` of type

  (`runAPICoverageFailure` reads `tc.FailureStatus` / `tc.FailureCode`
  with sensible defaults), so no harness change was needed.
- Files changed:

    http.StatusNotFound` and `FailureCode: yerr.CodeNotFound`)

- Verification run:
  * `gofmt -w .` → clean
  * `goimports` → not installed (consistent with prior iterations)
  * `go mod tidy` → no changes
  * `go vet ./...` → exit 0
  * `go test ./...` → all 9 packages PASS
  * `go test -race ./...` → all 9 packages PASS
  * `go test ./internal/cli -run TestAPICoverage -count=1 -v` →
    every subtest PASS, including the new
    `TestAPICoverage_RepresentativeFailure/API-0342/server-one`
    which exercises the 404 → CodeNotFound override end-to-end
  * `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`, `govulncheck`, `goreleaser` →
    not installed (documented in prior progress entries; no change
    this iteration)
- Results: 116/462 PRD stories now passing; CI-equivalent local
  checks all green.
- Remaining risks or follow-ups: None specific to this story. The
  next server/* peer (API-0343 `server-publicIp`) returns to the
  parameter-free GET shape established at API-0335..API-0337 /
  API-0341 and should keep the harness default 401 → CodeAuth.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **Activating a reserved harness override is a pure-data
    change.** API-0290's design header reserved 404 → CodeNotFound
    for the canonical `*-one` peer; API-0294 `project-one` chose
    not to act on it for tag-roster symmetry. API-0342
    `server-one` is the first peer to *act*, simply by setting
    `FailureStatus: http.StatusNotFound, FailureCode:
    yerr.CodeNotFound` in the struct literal — no harness or
    runner edit required. The two zero-default fields exist
    precisely for this kind of opt-in.
  - **`tc.FailureCode` must use the typed `yerr.Code` constant**
    (e.g. `yerr.CodeNotFound`), NOT a string literal. The struct
    field is `yerr.Code` (a defined string type) and the comparison
    in `runAPICoverageFailure` does `string(failCode)` for the
    stderr substring match. Using `"E_NOT_FOUND"` would compile
    (Go allows untyped string→named-string conversion in struct
    literals) but breaks the contract — always import via the
    `yerr "github.com/JuribaDev/yalla/internal/errors"` alias
    already in scope and reference the constant.
  - **The 404 override semantically belongs on the by-id peer of
    the tag whose call site most often encounters cold-cache
    fetches**, not necessarily the *first* `*-one` peer in the
    roster. project-one (API-0294) would have been the alphabetic
    first opportunity, but the project/* arc punted to keep its
    arc symmetric. server-one is a stronger fit because Dokploy
    server records are pinned to UUIDs an agent will frequently
    refetch on cold-cache restart, where 404 (record deleted
    between cache fill and fetch) is a more common runtime
    failure than 401 (process already proved auth). Future
    contributors picking the next "primary failure mode is
    not-found" peer should grep this entry's design rationale
    block first.
  - **Cross-tag `*-one` shape is now extensively documented.**
    By the time API-0342 lands, the by-id GET shape has been
    exercised at API-0008 `ai-one`, API-0021 `application-one`,
    API-0084 `compose-one`, API-0251 `organization-one`, and
    API-0294 `project-one`. Each shares the byte-for-byte wire
    contract (single required scalar query param, empty-object
    200 response, 401/404 in the failure surface). Future tags'
    `*-one` peers are pure copy-and-rename — only the ID field
    name and the per-tag fixture slug change.
  - **Forward-reference comments paid off here.** API-0335's
    opener block, plus API-0336/0337/0341's commentary, all
    explicitly named API-0342 `server-one` as the canonical home
    for the 404 override, which made the design decision a
    single grep instead of a re-derivation. The chain continues:
    this entry now names API-0343 `server-publicIp` for the
    parameter-free re-anchoring.

    declares.** API-0338 `server-create` carried seven required
    fields including a nullable `description` and an

    carries exactly one — a required `serverId` string scalar.
    This makes API-0344 the canonical reference for future
    "single-id POST removal" mutations across other tags
    (`*-remove`, `*-delete`, `*-archive` style endpoints), which
    is a recurring Dokploy idiom. Future contributors picking
    up a `*-remove` peer in any tag should grep this entry first
    before deriving the SampleBody shape, and should keep the
    SampleBody to the documented required field set rather than
    speculatively adding optional metadata.

    even when semantically by-id.** `server-remove` semantically
    operates on a serverId and could plausibly 404 on a missing
    record at runtime, but the embedded spec does not enumerate
    404 in its response set (200/400/401/403/500 only). The
    "exercise the documented contract, not a speculative future
    tightening" rule (reasserted at API-0337 `server-count`,
    API-0341 `server-getServerTime`, and API-0343
    `server-publicIp` for response *payload* shapes) applies
    equally to *failure* leg shapes: the API-0342 `server-one`
    404 → CodeNotFound override is reserved for endpoints that
    actually declare 404 in their spec, and pre-emptively
    overriding here would diverge from the embedded contract.
    Future `*-remove` peers should grep this paragraph before
    copying API-0342's failure-leg lines.
  - **Cross-shape diff-friendliness via shared slug roots.**
    The server/* roster now spans five shape families
    (parameter-free GET, single-required-query GET,
    multi-required-query GET, by-id GET with 404 override, and
    body mutation in two body-size variants). All ten cases
    share the `srv-cov-*` slug root with a per-case suffix
    encoding the operation slug + StoryID
    (`srv-cov-create-0338`, `srv-cov-getServerMetrics-0340`,
    `srv-cov-one-0342`, `srv-cov-remove-0344`, etc.). This makes
    a `git grep srv-cov-` instantly reveal the entire server/*
    fixture inventory and any accidental cross-tag leaks.
    Future tags should preserve this convention.
  - **Forward-reference chain remains the navigation backbone.**
    API-0343 named API-0344 as the "next body-mutation
    re-introduction"; this entry now names API-0345 as the next
    parameter-free GET re-anchor and API-0346/0347/0348 as the
    upcoming server/* mutation peers. The chain continues to
    make per-case design decisions a single `git grep "API-XXXX"`
    rather than a re-derivation. Future iterations should
    preserve this pattern — each new case should both
    back-reference its predecessor's design rationale and
    forward-reference at least one upcoming peer.
  - **Adding a body-mutation coverage entry remains a pure-data
    change** when the shape is documented in the embedded
    OpenAPI spec — no production code, registry, schema, or
    manifest edits are needed because the embedded OpenAPI
    document already advertises the operation. The harness's
    `runAPICoverageSuccess` reads `tc.SampleBody` and asserts

  `internal/cli/api_coverage_test.go`. Thirteenth entry in the server/*
  roster and the **fourth body-mutation peer** (after API-0338
  `server-create`, API-0344 `server-remove`, API-0346 `server-setup`).
- **Forward-reference correction**: API-0346's design block predicted
  this entry would be a "pure copy-and-rename" mirror of its single-
  required-`serverId` body. The embedded spec
  (`internal/api/data/openapi.json > /server.setupMonitoring > post`)
  proved that wrong: the body declares TWO required top-level fields,

  required leaves are: `metricsConfig.server.{refreshRate, port,
  token, urlCallback, retentionDays, cronJob, thresholds}` and
  `metricsConfig.server.thresholds.{cpu, memory}` and
  `metricsConfig.containers.{refreshRate, services}`. This is the
  **largest body shape on the server/* mutation roster** — strictly
  larger than API-0338's seven flat required fields. Re-anchors the
  API-0345 lesson that `internal/api/data/openapi.json` is the single
  source of truth.

  - `internal/cli/api_coverage_test.go` — appended API-0347 case at the
    end of `coveredAPIOperations`. Body fixture populates every required
    leaf per the spec.
  - `ralph/prd.json` — set API-0347 `passes: true` (note: stories live
    under top-level `userStories`, NOT a separate `apiStories` array).
- **Verification run**:
  - `gofmt -l .` — clean (no diff).
  - `go mod tidy` — clean.
  - `go vet ./...` — pass.
  - `go test ./...` — all packages `ok`.
  - `go test -race ./...` — all packages `ok`.
  - `go test ./internal/cli/ -run 'TestAPICoverage' -count=1` — pass.
- **Tools NOT available locally** (unchanged baseline): `goimports`,
  `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`, `govulncheck`, `goreleaser`.
- **Remaining risks / follow-ups**: API-0348 `server-update` is the
  next pending server/* mutation; do NOT blindly mirror API-0347 — its
  `update`-shaped schemas typically declare many optional + a few
  required fields, so re-verify against the embedded spec first.
  API-0349 `server-validate` is a single-required-`serverId` query GET
  and should mirror API-0345 `server-security`. API-0350
  `server-withSSHKey` is unknown until verified.
- **Learnings for future iterations**:
  - **Forward-reference comments lie when the spec disagrees.** The
    API-0345 lesson held: API-0346 promised API-0347 would be "pure
    copy-and-rename"; it turned out to be the largest body in the tag.
    Always re-verify against `internal/api/data/openapi.json` first.
  - **PRD shape gotcha**: all stories (user + API) live under a single
    top-level `userStories` array in `ralph/prd.json`. There is no
    separate `apiStories` array, even though the agent prompt and PRD
    summary text talk about API stories as a category. A naive
    `for s in d['apiStories']` loop will silently no-op and write the
    file unchanged. Use `for s in d['userStories']` and filter by
    `id` prefix or `type == 'api-operation'` if needed.
  - **Body-fixture token literals**: when an OpenAPI body declares a
    `token` field (e.g. `metricsConfig.server.token` here), pick a
    fixture literal that does NOT match the test harness's resolved
    `--token` value (`test-token-value`) and does NOT match any
    `Authorization:` / `X-API-Key:` / `?token=` / `?api_key=`
    redactor pattern, so the round-trip body-equality assertion in
    `runAPICoverageSuccess` is not corrupted by `output.NewRedactor`.
    A `fixture-token-<slug>-<storyID>` shape is safe.
  - **Use IANA-reserved domains for fixture URLs** (`example.invalid`,
    not a real-looking domain) so the literal can never be confused
    with a production callback if it leaks into a log.
  - **Numeric leaves should encode schema intent** (e.g. port 9100 =
    node_exporter default, 80% CPU/memory thresholds, 7-day retention)
    so the fixture documents the field's purpose at a glance for the
    next reviewer.
  - **No 404 on server/* mutations stays load-bearing**: the per-tag
    convention reasserted at API-0335..API-0346 holds again here. Body
    mutations on the server/* tag enumerate 200/400/401/403/500 only;
    404 stays reserved for the by-id GET peer (API-0342 `server-one`).
    Failure-leg fields stay omitted; harness defaults (401 → CodeAuth)
    apply.

    flagging the namespace-inheritance rule and the spec

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **Tag-opening entries establish a fresh per-tag fixture-isolation
    namespace.** API-0351 opens settings/* and establishes
    `set-cov-*` orthogonal to all prior namespaces. The pattern is
    documented in two places (the new entry's comment block and the
    Codebase Patterns section's namespace-isolation rule reasserted
    at API-0335..API-0350) so future tag-openers can copy the
    convention verbatim without spelunking through 5,000+ lines of
    test fixtures.
  - **The settings tag has no 404 response** because settings is a
    singleton, not a by-id resource. This is structurally different
    from server/*, project/*, organization/*, etc., which all have
    `*-one` peers. The 404 → CodeNotFound override stays reserved
    for those `*-one` peers; settings/* peers (this one and future
    API-0352..) all default to 401 → CodeAuth via the harness.

    convention.** Even when the spec marks a field optional
    (`letsEncryptEmail`, `https`), populating it with a

    serialiser's optional-field branch on the wire and gives future
    schema-validator wiring more surface area to assert against.

    `certificateType` is set to `"none"` rather than `"letsencrypt"`
    or `"custom"` because the latter two imply cert-provisioning
    side effects the fixture cannot honour. This generalises: when
    a required enum has a "no-op" member, pick it.

- Spec re-verified against
  `internal/api/data/openapi.json > /settings.checkGPUStatus > get`
  per the API-0345..API-0351 forward-reference lesson:
  zero request body, a single **OPTIONAL** query parameter
  `serverId` (string, **no `required: true`**), no path parameters.
  Responses 200/400/401/403/404/500. Structurally byte-identical to
  `/server.validate > get` modulo (a) the `tag` array and (b) the
  `serverId` `required` flag, verified at story authoring time via
  `diff <(jq -S '.paths["/server.validate"].get | del(.operationId)' …)
  <(jq -S '.paths["/settings.checkGPUStatus"].get | del(.operationId)' …)`,
  which produced exactly two-line drift. The 200 schema is `{}`
  with `additionalProperties: false`, matching every prior covered
  peer.
- **Forward-reference correction surfaced.** API-0351's comment had
  predicted API-0352 would be a parameter-free GET (cf. API-0006
  `ai-getAll`, API-0350 `server-withSSHKey`). The re-verification
  turned up a single-OPTIONAL-query-param shape instead — closer to
  API-0349 `server-validate` but with the `required` constraint
  relaxed. This is the latest iteration of the "always re-verify the
  spec before mirroring" lesson (API-0345/0347/0348/0349/0350 each
  surfaced the same correction). The new entry's "Forward-reference
  correction" comment block records this in-place so future
  contributors see the trail.
- Fixture decisions:
  - `serverId`: `"set-cov-checkGPUStatus-0352"` (per-case fixture
    token, deterministic-but-clearly-fake; populating the optional
    parameter exercises the query-string wire path through the raw
    API executor and keeps this case distinct from the parameter-
    free GET cohort).
- **Files changed**:
  - `internal/cli/api_coverage_test.go` — appended the API-0352 case
    after the API-0351 entry. The block forward-references API-0353
    `settings-cleanAll` (the next pending settings/* peer, a POST
    with `requestBody.required = false` and an optional `serverId`

  - `ralph/progress.txt` — this entry.

  - `gofmt -w .` — clean.

  - `go test ./...` — all packages pass.
  - `go test -race ./...` — all packages pass (`internal/cli` 2.606s).
  - `go test ./internal/cli/ -run 'TestAPICoverage_.*/API-0352' -v` —
    all five harness subtests pass for API-0352.

  `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`, `govulncheck`, `goreleaser`. Skipped
  silently per the existing convention; `internal/cli/AGENTS.md`
  documents this.

  pending settings/* story is API-0353 `settings-cleanAll`. Per the
  forward-reference lesson, do NOT mirror this single-query-param GET
  shape — re-verify against
  `internal/api/data/openapi.json > /settings.cleanAll > post` and
  inherit the `set-cov-*` namespace established at API-0351.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **The `required` flag is metadata, not wire shape.** OpenAPI's
    `required: true` on a parameter only tells the client whether
    pre-flight validation should reject a missing input — it does not
    change the HTTP handshake when the parameter IS supplied. So
    `/server.validate` (required serverId) and
    `/settings.checkGPUStatus` (optional serverId) are byte-identical
    on the wire when both fixtures populate `serverId`. The harness's
    success-leg round trip exercises the populated path either way;
    the distinction matters only for human contributors deciding
    whether to populate the fixture (always populate for query
    parameters — leaving them unset would degrade the case to the
    parameter-free GET cohort and lose the query-forwarding wire
    assertion).
  - **Forward-reference predictions can be wrong; the comments must
    record both the prediction AND the correction.** API-0351
    confidently predicted "parameter-free GET" but the spec showed a
    single-optional-query-param GET. The new entry documents the
    correction inline in a "Forward-reference correction" block so
    the next contributor sees both the original guess and the
    verified shape — this preserves the lesson without erasing the
    history of how it was found.
  - **`apiCoverageCase` literals use 2-tab indentation, NOT 3.**
    A file-bytes inspection (`od -c`) confirmed each case body
    indents fields at `\t\t`, the closing `},` at `\t`, and the
    slice's outer `}` is flush left. An earlier Edit attempt with
    3-tab indentation failed to match because the Read tool's
    line-number prefix can visually inflate apparent indentation
    depth — when in doubt, run
    `awk 'NR>=L1 && NR<=L2' FILE | od -c` to confirm raw bytes
    before authoring the Edit `old_string`.

    fixture choice is to populate the body anyway. Leaving the body
    unset would degrade the case to the parameter-free POST cohort
    (no Content-Type assertion) and lose the body-forwarding round
    trip that distinguishes this shape from query-only or path-only
    siblings. Populating the body keeps the harness's success-leg
    `Content-Type: application/json` and JSON-equality body
    assertions meaningful.

    collision-safe across tags because the tag prefix is mandatory;
    verify against neighbouring tag rosters (no `srv-cov-*`,
    `proj-cov-*`, `org-cov-*`, `compose-cov-*`, `app-cov-*`,
    `ai-cov-*` reuse) when adding the first few entries of a new tag,
    then trust the prefix for subsequent peers in the same tag.
  - Optional-body POSTs whose response set lacks 404 are common in
    fleet-wide / scope-by-optional-id verbs (`cleanAll`,
    `cleanAllDeploymentQueue`, `cleanDockerBuilder`, …). The per-tag
    opener convention that reserves 404 → CodeNotFound for `*-one`
    by-id peers does not even apply — falling through to the harness
    default 401 → CodeAuth is the right call.

  re-verify against `internal/api/data/openapi.json >
  /settings.cleanDockerBuilder > post` before authoring. The
  `clean*` verb family in the settings/* tag has already shown
  three different body shapes (none, optional `{serverId}`, and the
  upcoming API-0355 unknown), proving the per-operation spec is the
  only authoritative source.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **No-body POST is a distinct sub-cohort.** Until this story, every
    POST entry in `coveredAPIOperations` had a `SampleBody`. API-0354
    establishes the no-body-POST convention: omit `SampleBody`,
    `SampleQuery`, and `SamplePathParams` together; the harness's
    `if len(tc.SampleBody) > 0` guard at `runAPICoverageSuccess`
    skips the Content-Type and body round-trip assertions, while
    method, path, Authorization header, empty query string,
    schema_version, data.operation_id, data.method, and data.status
    all remain asserted. This is the canonical form for a future
    `clean*`-family no-body peer.
  - **`requestBody.required = false` ≠ no `requestBody`.** API-0353
    had an optional body schema (`requestBody.required = false`
    carrying `{serverId}`); API-0354 has no `requestBody` field at
    all. The two shapes both fall under the same agent contract
    (`yalla api call <op> --input '{}' --json` works for both), but
    on the wire only the API-0353 case forwards a body, and only
    API-0353's success-leg test asserts a body round-trip.
    Re-verifying the spec against the embedded openapi.json before
    authoring is the only way to disambiguate — this is the
    seventh consecutive iteration of the same lesson
    (API-0345/0347/0348/0349/0350/0352/0354).
  - **Fixture-slug reservation is still useful for no-body POSTs.**
    Even when no fixture-token literal reaches the wire, reserving
    `set-cov-<slug>-<storyID>` keeps future contributors' cross-
    reference grep working — a contributor authoring API-0355 can
    `rg 'set-cov-cleanAllDeploymentQueue'` and find this entry as
    the canonical no-body POST exemplar.

    (query-shaped GET precedent), not this entry.

    (`bitbucket-create`, `bitbucket-testConnection`,
    `bitbucket-update`) with response set 200/400/401/403/500
    (the canonical mutation set, **without 404**). They should
    consult the cross-tag `*-create` / `*-update` precedents

    API-0338 `server-create`) and re-derive each required
    field from `internal/api/data/openapi.json` rather than
    cargo-culting from sibling slugs.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **Tag-opener entries are the most expensive to author** —
    they need to enumerate every prior namespace
    (`admin-cov-*`, `ai-cov-*`, `app-cov-*`, `backup-cov-*`,
    `compose-cov-*`, `deployment-cov-*`, `org-cov-*`,
    `proj-cov-*`, `srv-cov-*`, `set-cov-*` so far) and
    explicitly call out which namespace the new tag inherits
    from, plus enumerate every forthcoming peer the new tag
    will spawn so future contributors know where to grep.
    Subsequent peers in the same tag are cheaper because they
    can back-reference their tag-opener.
  - **Compact tag prefix selection:** when picking a
    `<prefix>-cov-*` token base for a new tag, prefer the
    shortest unambiguous abbreviation (matching `ai`, `app`,
    `srv`, `org`, `proj`, `set`). For `bitbucket`, the
    two-letter `bb-` is unambiguous against every prior
    namespace — `bit-` would collide with `bitbucket` itself
    if a future feature needs a sub-namespace, and the full
    `bitbucket-cov-*` would violate the compact-prefix
    convention. Future tag-openers should similarly pick the
    shortest unambiguous abbreviation.
  - **Bitbucket-specific spec verification observation:** the
    `bitbucket` tag has seven operations split 3 GET / 4 POST.
    The three GETs all carry 404 in their response set; the
    four POSTs do not (canonical mutation 200/400/401/403/500
    set). This split is per-operation, not per-tag, and
    matches the cross-tag pattern observed at every prior
    roster — verify each operation's response set
    individually rather than assuming a tag-wide rule.
  - **Forward-reference lesson re-applied:** the next story
    in the bitbucket/* roster, API-0052 `bitbucket-create`,
    pivots onto a POST with a request body — do **not** assume
    the body shape mirrors any other tag's `*-create` solely
    because the slug matches; consult API-0292 / API-0338 for
    the flat scalar-only mutation precedent, then re-derive
    each required field from
    `internal/api/data/openapi.json > /bitbucket.create > post`.
  - `goimports`, `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`, `govulncheck`,
    and `goreleaser` remain not installed locally and continue
    to be documented as missing rather than silently skipped —
    same status as every prior tag-opener story.

## 2026-05-08 - API-0052 - Cover bitbucket-create (POST /bitbucket.create)
- What was implemented: per-operation contract coverage for the
  `bitbucket-create` POST mutation. This is the second bitbucket/*
  story (after API-0051 `bitbucket-bitbucketProviders` opened the
  tag with a parameter-free GET) and the **first mutation** in the
  bitbucket/* roster — therefore the entry that *opens* the
  `bb-cov-*` per-tag fixture-isolation namespace reserved by
  API-0051's design header.
- The operation is a parameter-free POST with a required
  `application/json` request body whose schema declares nine
  top-level scalar fields:
    * REQUIRED scalars (2): `authId`, `name`.
    * OPTIONAL scalars (7, all plain string): `bitbucketId`,
      `bitbucketUsername`, `bitbucketEmail`, `appPassword`,
      `apiToken`, `bitbucketWorkspaceName`, `gitProviderId`.
  No nested objects, no arrays, no enums, no `anyOf [string, null]`
  nullables — the **flattest mutation body in the cross-tag
  roster so far**, strictly stringly-typed. Response set
  200/400/401/403/500 (no 404 — canonical mutation set, matching
  every prior `*-create` peer: API-0002 `ai-create`, API-0040
  `backup-create`, API-0292 `project-create`, API-0338
  `server-create`).
- Files changed:
  - `internal/cli/api_coverage_test.go` — appended a 154-line
    apiCoverageCase struct literal (entry #135, sorted by StoryID
    between API-0051 `bitbucket-bitbucketProviders` and API-0066
    `compose-cancelDeployment` per the diff-friendliness rule).
    Carries `SampleBody` populated per the every-optional-populated
    convention; fixture token base `bb-cov-create-0052` opens the
    `bb-cov-*` namespace and pre-reserves the slugs
    `bb-cov-getBranches-0053`, `bb-cov-getRepos-0054`,
    `bb-cov-one-0055`, `bb-cov-testConn-0056`,
    `bb-cov-update-0057` for the forthcoming bitbucket/* peers.
    Failure-leg defaults exercise the canonical 401 → CodeAuth
    mapping. The header comment explicitly forbids cargo-culting
    this entry's flat-string-only shape into the upcoming
    bitbucket/* mutation peers (API-0056 `bitbucket-testConnection`,
    API-0057 `bitbucket-update`) without per-operation re-derivation
    from the embedded spec.
  - `ralph/prd.json` — flipped API-0052 `passes` to `true`.
  - `ralph/progress.txt` — this entry.

  - `gofmt -w .`                           → clean.

                                             (documented).
  - `go mod tidy`                          → clean (no diff).

    -v` → all five subtests green (registry, schema, manifest,
    success round-trip, representative failure).
- Results: API coverage advances from 146 → 147 passing /
  462 total (315 remaining). The bitbucket/* tag now has its
  first mutation covered alongside the GET kickoff; five
  bitbucket/* peers remain uncovered (API-0053..API-0057).
- Remaining risks or follow-ups: API-0053
  `bitbucket-getBitbucketBranches` (GET) is the next story by
  PRD ordering. Per the spec it carries **three query
  parameters** (the largest GET parameter count in the
  bitbucket/* tag), so the next contributor should consult
  API-0033 `application-readTraefikConfig` for the
  query-shaped GET precedent — **not this entry**, which is a
  flat-scalar-only POST mutation. Future contributors must
  re-verify each bitbucket/* peer's shape per the
  API-0345..API-0363 forward-reference lesson.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **Flat-string-only mutation sub-shape:** the bitbucket/*
    `*-create` peer is the first cross-tag mutation entry that
    is **strictly stringly-typed at the body's top level** —
    no number fields (unlike API-0338 `server-create`'s
    `port: number`), no enum-pinned scalars (unlike API-0338's
    `serverType: "deploy"`), and no `anyOf [string, null]`
    nullables (unlike API-0292 `project-create`'s `description`
    and API-0338's `description` / `sshKeyId`). This is a
    distinct sub-shape inside the broader flat-scalar-only
    mutation cohort and worth flagging as a precedent for any
    future POST that turns out to have only string scalars.
    The flat-string-only shape is **per-operation** and must
    not be assumed for the upcoming bitbucket/* mutation peers
    (API-0056 `bitbucket-testConnection`, API-0057
    `bitbucket-update`) without re-derivation.
  - **Secret-looking field names in mutation bodies:** when a
    Dokploy POST body carries fields whose names *look* like
    credentials (`appPassword`, `apiToken`, `bearerToken`, etc.)
    the fixture values must be obviously-fake (suffixed
    `-fixture` and prefixed with the per-case fixture token
    base) so a casual reader or future automated secret
    scanner can immediately tell they are coverage fixtures.
    The harness's `output.NewRedactor(flags.Token)` only
    scrubs the explicit `--token` value plus the well-known
    transport patterns (`Authorization:`, `X-Auth-Token:`,
    `?token=`); it does NOT match embedded JSON keys named
    `appPassword` / `apiToken`, so these literals round-trip
    through the wire body unchanged. Future mutation entries
    with credential-shaped optional scalars should follow the
    same `<token>-<fieldname>-fixture` literal convention.
  - **`@example.test` mailbox literal:** for body fields typed
    as email-shaped strings, RFC 6761 reserves
    `*.example.test` for documentation; `bitbucketEmail`
    carries `bb-cov-create-0052@example.test` so the fixture
    cannot be mistaken for a real mailbox. Future mutation
    entries with email-shaped scalars should follow the same
    `<token>@example.test` convention rather than a freeform
    string.
  - **Tag-mutation-opener entries:** authoring the first
    mutation in a tag is the second-most-expensive entry shape
    after the tag opener itself — it must (a) inherit the
    `<prefix>-cov-*` namespace from the tag opener, (b) enumerate
    every cross-tag flat-scalar-only mutation precedent
    (API-0292 / API-0338 in this case), (c) explicitly forbid
    cargo-culting from sibling tag namespaces, (d) re-derive
    every body field from the embedded spec rather than
    mirroring the cross-tag precedent's body shape, and
    (e) pre-reserve fixture-token slugs for every forthcoming
    peer in the same tag so the namespace stays diff-traceable.
    Subsequent mutations in the same tag are cheaper because
    they back-reference this entry.
  - **No 404 on `/bitbucket.create`** — canonical mutation
    response set, matching every prior `*-create` peer
    (API-0002 `ai-create`, API-0040 `backup-create`, API-0292
    `project-create`, API-0338 `server-create`). Per the
    per-tag opener convention reasserted at API-0051's
    bitbucket/* design header, 404 → CodeNotFound stays
    reserved for the canonical by-id peer API-0055
    `bitbucket-one`.
  - `goimports`, `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`, `govulncheck`,
    and `goreleaser` remain not installed locally and continue
    to be documented as missing rather than silently skipped —
    same status as every prior coverage story.

  - **Single-required-only query GET is the simplest cell.**
    API-0054 establishes the simplest-possible query-bearing
    GET shape in the bitbucket/* coverage matrix: one required
    string scalar, no optional siblings, no request body. The
    harness fixture is one map entry. This is a structural
    counterpoint not just to API-0053's 3-param shape but to
    the broader query-shape spectrum across the registry —
    API-0035 `application-search` (11 optional, 0 required),
    API-0053 `bitbucket-getBranches` (2 required + 1 optional),
    API-0054 here (1 required + 0 optional). Future
    single-required-only query GETs in any tag (API-0055
    `bitbucket-one` is next in line) can grep this entry for
    the canonical handling.
  - **Every-optional-populated rule is a NO-OP when no optionals
    exist.** API-0010 / API-0014 / API-0249 / API-0292 / API-0297
    / API-0052 / API-0053 each populated optional fields
    alongside required ones so the wire envelope was
    exhaustive. API-0054 exercises a degenerate case of the
    same rule: when the spec declares no optional siblings,
    the minimum-required envelope IS the whole envelope. The
    rule is preserved by virtue of the spec, not by additional
    fixture work. This generalises the every-optional-populated
    rule from "always populate optionals" to "always exercise
    the full envelope per the spec".
  - **`bb-cov-*` namespace expansion continues.** API-0051
    reserved `bb-cov-providers-0051` (no fixture), API-0052
    consumed `bb-cov-create-0052-*-fixture` for body fields,
    API-0053 consumed `bb-cov-getBranches-0053-*` for query
    values, and API-0054 now consumes `bb-cov-getRepos-0054-*`.
    Forthcoming bitbucket/* peers (API-0055..API-0057) inherit
    the `bb-cov-*` namespace per the per-tag fixture-isolation
    rule established at API-0246 `organization-active`.
    The reserved slugs `bb-cov-one-0055`, `bb-cov-testConn-0056`,
    `bb-cov-update-0057` remain reserved with no collisions.
  - **No new harness code needed.** Confirms the API-XXXX
    coverage pattern: every Dokploy OpenAPI operation can be
    covered by appending exactly one struct literal to
    `coveredAPIOperations` — the registry, schema, manifest,
    success round-trip, and representative-failure assertions
    flow automatically through the shared harness. The OpenAPI
    registry is the single source of truth; adding a coverage
    case never requires touching the registry, manifest
    emitter, or schema emitter.

  `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`, `govulncheck`, `goreleaser`.
- **Remaining risks / follow-ups**:
  - The harness still does not gate on `required`-ness -- it
    forwards whatever `SampleQuery` carries. That is the
    intentional contract (the executor is a thin pass-through and
    Dokploy's upstream handler enforces required-ness), but a
    future story that wants to assert REQUIRED-parameter
    enforcement at the executor layer will need a dedicated
    sub-suite outside the coverage harness.
  - 400 (CodeInvalidInput) is the operation's most distinguishing
    failure mode given the REQUIRED `path` parameter (Dokploy
    rejects malformed paths or paths that escape the allowed
    Traefik configuration directory), but the coverage harness
    keeps the canonical 401 -> CodeAuth representative for parity
    with every prior settings/* GET entry. A future story that
    wants 400-specific assertions for this operation can override
    `FailureStatus`/`FailureCode` explicitly without touching
    the harness.
- **Learnings for future iterations**:
  - The `required` axis is its own dimension on the parameter
    sub-axis -- even when two adjacent parameter-bearing settings/*
    GETs both declare a single query parameter, one can be
    REQUIRED and the other OPTIONAL. API-0381 is the first
    settings/* GET to carry a REQUIRED query parameter; the
    immediately preceding peer API-0380 carried only an OPTIONAL
    `serverId`. Direct spec inspection at
    `/settings.readTraefikFile > get > parameters` is the only
    way to surface this -- slug-prefix and parameter-count
    similarity are not sufficient signals.
  - When an operation declares MULTIPLE query parameters,
    populate ALL of them in `SampleQuery` (not just the
    REQUIRED ones) so the success-leg `r.URL.Query()` re-read
    exercises end-to-end forwarding for the full parameter
    surface. The harness ignores empty maps but does iterate
    every key the case provides, so a partial `SampleQuery`
    silently skips the missing-key forwarding assertion.
  - The fixture slug convention extends naturally to
    multi-parameter cases: append a `-<param>` suffix to the
    canonical `<tag-prefix>-cov-<opID>-<storyID>` slug
    (`set-cov-readTraefikFile-0381-path` and
    `set-cov-readTraefikFile-0381-server`) so each parameter
    has its own unique literal. The hyphenated suffix keeps the
    fixture-namespace lookup grep-friendly across the test file.
  - The next case in the settings/* roster per PRD ordering is
    API-0382 `settings-readWebServerTraefikConfig`. The
    forward-reference lesson (parameter axis, response-set axis,
    request-body axis) reasserted at API-0345..API-0381 still
    applies -- the next contributor must re-verify against
    `internal/api/data/openapi.json >
    /settings.readWebServerTraefikConfig > get` before assuming
    any field is identical to this entry. The `read*` slug
    family continues to straddle every sub-axis.

  - **Per-tag arc-closing entries should explicitly state the closure.** When the entry being added is the last pending story in its tag (verified via `prd.json` filter on `apiOperation.tag`), the design-rationale header should call this out and explicitly *not* open a forward-reference reservation for future peers, mirroring the inverse of API-0051..API-0055's "Future contributors picking up..." paragraphs. This keeps the breadcrumb trail honest — the next contributor reading API-0057's header should not search for a phantom "API-0058 bitbucket-*" continuation.
  - **Update vs create body-shape divergence is a per-operation re-verification target.** API-0052 `bitbucket-create` requires `authId` + `name` (allocates a fresh `bitbucketId` under an `authId`); API-0057 `bitbucket-update` requires `bitbucketId` + `gitProviderId` + `name` (binds an existing `bitbucketId` and `gitProviderId`). The two POSTs share neither their required-set nor their full optional-set (`organizationId` is unique to update; `authId` is unique to create). Future `*-update` peers should grep this entry for the precedent.

Per-operation re-verification is mandatory; copying the field name from a sibling without re-checking the spec would silently break payload validation. The API-0353..API-0362 settings/* `clean*` body-axis reminder (originally documented at API-0055) generalizes to this pattern.
  - **Harness-default 401 → CodeAuth pre-reservation pattern.** API-0056's design-rationale header explicitly forward-referenced API-0057 ("expected to follow the same harness-default convention"). That reservation was honored verbatim — the entry sets neither `FailureStatus` nor `FailureCode`, falling through to the harness default. Future contributors writing forward-references should make them as concrete as API-0056 did (specific operation ID + specific failure-code expectation), not vague hints, so the next iteration can consume the slot without re-derivation.
  - **Per-tag namespace exhaustion.** The bitbucket/* `bb-cov-*` namespace is now closed (slugs: `bb-cov-providers-0051`, `bb-cov-create-0052-*`, `bb-cov-getBranches-0053-*`, `bb-cov-getRepos-0054-*`, `bb-cov-one-0055-*`, `bb-cov-testConn-0056-*`, `bb-cov-update-0057-*`). No future story may write into `bb-cov-*` per the per-tag isolation rule established at API-0246 and reasserted by the API-0051 bitbucket/* kickoff header.

    (API-0363..API-0369) with a single POST, then the GET
    cohort resumed (API-0371..API-0382, twelve entries),
    then API-0383 broke it again with a POST. The
    settings/* roster therefore has at least three verb
    pivots so far. Per-operation re-verification stays the
    only safe way to determine the next entry's verb; do not
    assume verb continuity even within a same-prefix slug
    family.
  - **`reload*` actions are platform-wide, not per-resource.**
    Like the `clean*` family, the `reload*` family operates
    on a controller-owned global service (Redis, the Dokploy
    server itself, Traefik) rather than a per-tenant resource;
    this is why 404 is absent from the response set
    (there is no per-resource lookup that could miss). The
    optional `serverId` on `reloadTraefik` (API-0385)
    optionally scopes the reload to a remote node but does
    not make the operation per-resource in the
    has-an-id-and-can-404 sense. Future `reload*` contributors
    should not introduce 404 -> CodeNotFound coverage for
    this family.
  - **The empty-body, parameter-free, no-`requestBody` POST
    shape requires ZERO production code changes -- only the
    `apiCoverageCase` literal is needed, exactly mirroring
    the API-0370 minimal-literal pattern. The harness's POST
    branch with `len(SampleBody) == 0` skips the
    `Content-Type` and body-round-trip assertions per the
    `if len(tc.SampleBody) > 0` guard inside
    `runAPICoverageSuccess`, and the failure leg defaults to
    401 -> CodeAuth when `FailureStatus == 0`.

    (POST /certificates.create) -- a sibling certificates/*
    mutation that should consume a `cert-cov-create-0059-*`
    fixture-token namespace, but per-operation re-verification

    in the certificates/* tag and should claim the 404 ->
    CodeNotFound representative-failure slot reserved by this
    entry's design-rationale header.
- **Learnings for future iterations**:
  - **Minimal-literal GET shape is the canonical opener for a
    list-style tag arc.** When a tag's first pending entry is
    a parameter-free, body-free GET (e.g. `<tag>-all` /
    `<tag>-list`), the case literal should consist of nothing
    but `StoryID`, `OperationID`, `Method`, `Path`, `Tag`, and
    a design-rationale comment block — every `Sample*` field
    omitted, defaulting to 200 / `{}` for success and 401 ->
    CodeAuth for failure. This matches the minimal-literal
    pattern established at API-0378/API-0379 and most
    recently consumed by API-0383 `settings-reloadRedis`. The
    no-input-flag path is exercised because
    `buildCoverageInputArgs` short-circuits to an empty slice
    when no `Sample*` fields are populated.
  - **Tag-arc-opener entries must explicitly nominate a 404 ->
    CodeNotFound holder.** When opening a new tag arc whose
    PRD priority list contains both a list-GET (`<tag>-all`)
    and a by-id-GET (`<tag>-one`), the list-GET opener must
    explicitly reserve the 404 -> CodeNotFound
    representative-failure slot for the upcoming
    `<tag>-one` peer (this is exactly what API-0055
    `bitbucket-one` did for the bitbucket/* tag). Reserving
    the slot in the opener — rather than letting it default
    out at the by-id peer — keeps the per-tag failure-leg
    distribution legible and prevents a future
    `<tag>-one` contributor from accidentally consuming the
    harness-default 401 -> CodeAuth slot.
  - **StoryID-sorted insertion catches comment-anchor
    ambiguity.** The `coveredAPIOperations` slice is kept
    sorted by StoryID for diff-friendliness. Inserting
    API-0058 between API-0057 (line 2569) and API-0066
    (line 2570) required matching a unique anchor — the
    bare `SuccessResponse: ` + "`" + "{}" + "`" + `,
	},
	{` pattern
    appears many times in the file, so the edit had to
    include enough of the API-0057 closing context (the
    `bb-cov-update-0057-organizationId` literal and its
    trailing comment block) to disambiguate. Future
    contributors editing into the middle of the slice should
    anchor on the prior entry's distinctive last lines, not
    on the generic struct-closer pattern.
  - **Indentation-of-body-vs-comment trap.** The Read tool's
    `cat -n` format prepends `<lineno>\t` so every line in a
    Read result *appears* to have one extra leading tab.
    The actual struct body uses single-tab indentation
    (`\t` for braces, `\t\t` for fields), not the apparent
    double-tab indentation. Edit calls must strip the Read
    line-number prefix before constructing `old_string` /
    `new_string`. A first attempt with double-tab indentation
    failed with "String to replace not found in file"; the
    fix was to verify the actual byte representation via
    `ctx_execute_file` + `repr(line)` before retrying.

    recently consumed by API-0383). When two adjacent

    header should explicitly call out the structural identity
    so the contributor of the third entry (API-0385) is on
    notice that the no-body shape is *not* a slug-prefix

    shape rule earns its keep on every entry, not just on

    onboarding for the next contributor; they should always

    The harness's POST branch with `len(SampleBody) == 0`
    skips the `Content-Type` and body-round-trip assertions
    (per the `if len(tc.SampleBody) > 0` guard inside
    `runAPICoverageSuccess`). For no-body, no-parameter POSTs
    the entire literal is just five fields plus the comment
    block — the marginal cost of adding a new entry to the
    slice is essentially zero. This keeps the per-entry
    review burden focused on the comment block (which
    captures the spec-re-verification trail and the
    cross-references) rather than on case-specific fixture
    plumbing.

    `clu-cov-*` namespace and **must not** back-reference the now-
    closed `cert-cov-*` namespace per the per-tag isolation rule.
- **Learnings for future iterations**:
  - **Per-tag forecast pays off.** API-0058's design-rationale header
    forecast all four certificates/* failure-leg slot assignments
    (list-all → harness default; create → harness default; by-id GET
    → 404 override; by-id remove → harness default). Each subsequent
    entry (API-0059, API-0060, API-0061) consumed exactly the
    pre-reserved slot with no re-litigation of the family choice.

    same forecast at the opener so the per-operation re-verification
    on later peers is just a spec sanity check, not a fresh design
    debate.

    `bitbucket-remove`, API-0298 `project-remove`, API-0344

    Even though "delete a thing that doesn't exist" feels like the
    canonical 404 case, the API instead surfaces it as a generic
    400/500 in practice. Per the contract-first rule, the test
    asserts the harness default (401 → CodeAuth) rather than
    inventing a 404 path the spec doesn't sanction. This is the
    standing reminder that the per-tag failure-leg override cohort
    is GET-by-id readers, not delete mutations.
  - **Tag-arc closer hygiene.** When the final entry on a tag arc
    lands, the progress.txt entry should call out the 4/4 (or N/N)
    completion explicitly so the next iteration immediately sees the
    namespace is closed and a fresh `<newtag>-cov-*` namespace must
    be opened.
