- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The `reload*` slug-prefix sub-roster in settings/* now spans three peers
    (API-0383 reloadRedis, API-0384 reloadServer, API-0385 reloadTraefik) and
    splits across the request-body axis: API-0383/0384 are no-body POSTs,
    API-0385 is the first `reload*` peer with an OPTIONAL body carrying an

    the same response set. API-0353 `settings-cleanAll` is the canonical

    use a JSON `true`/`false` literal rather than a fixture-string
    token for the boolean axis.

  `toggle*` peer in settings/* and the hand-off forecast for
  API-0390 was double-checked against the embedded OpenAPI doc.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - When the inner schema declares a `required: ["..."]` array,
    the success-leg fixture *must* populate every required
    field. Compare API-0388 (no inner-required → `{}` would have
    been valid) vs API-0389 (`enable` is required → `{}` would
    fail spec validation). The harness only checks a JSON
    round-trip on the wire, but a future stricter validator
    (or a Dokploy-side reject) would punish a missing required
    field.
  - The `<tag>-cov-<slug>-<storyID>` fixture-token base remains
    the namespace contract even when the inner schema has no
    string field to carry the slug onto the wire. In that case
    (like API-0389) the slug only appears in the closing
    forward-reference comment; the wire payload is just the
    minimal required shape. This matches the precedent set by
    API-0353/API-0383/API-0384 where the body axis was
    no-body / optional-only / minimal.
  - 400 → CodeInvalidInput is *technically* available for any
    operation whose inner schema declares a `required` array
    (a missing required field would 400), but the catalogue
    convention reserves 400 for stories whose coverage burden
    uniquely hinges on payload-shape validation
    (multi-field cross-validation, conditional `oneOf`/`anyOf`,
    length-bounded strings). A single-required-boolean toggle
    stays on the canonical 401 → CodeAuth representative.

  are likely shared, but per-operation re-verification
  remains mandatory.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The `update*` slug-prefix family within settings/*
    starts at API-0390 and runs contiguously through
    API-0397 per PRD ordering
    (`updateDockerCleanup`, `updateLogCleanup`,
    `updateMiddlewareTraefikConfig`, `updateServer`,
    `updateServerIp`, `updateTraefikConfig`,
    `updateTraefikFile`, `updateTraefikPorts`). Eight
    consecutive `update*` peers gives ample
    opportunity for axis pivots; do not assume any
    one entry's shape carries over.
  - When the inner schema declares a string-typed
    property (e.g. `serverId` here), the per-case
    fixture-isolation slug
    (`set-cov-<slug>-<storyID>`) should be carried
    on the wire via that property — restoring the
    API-0386/API-0387/API-0388 convention that
    API-0389 was forced to omit (its inner schema
    had only a `boolean` property). This keeps
    successive fixtures distinguishable on the wire
    even when the structural shape (verb, outer-body
    requirement, response set) is identical.
  - When an OPTIONAL field is structurally
    unnecessary (the inner `required` array does not
    name it) but exercising it improves coverage,
    populate it deliberately and document the
    coverage rationale in the case comment. Here
    `serverId` is OPTIONAL but populated to (a)
    exercise the mixed-type boolean+string
    serialiser branch, (b) surface the per-case slug
    on the wire, and (c) keep the fixture
    distinguishable from a hypothetical degenerate
    boolean-only payload that would otherwise be
    structurally indistinguishable from API-0389's
    wire shape.

    `apiCoverageCase` entry for `API-0391 / settings-updateLogCleanup`.
    `Method = http.MethodPost`, `Path = /settings.updateLogCleanup`,
    `Tag = settings`. `SampleBody` carries the lone REQUIRED inner
    property `cronExpression` (`anyOf: [{type:"string"},{type:"null"}]`)
    as a non-null string of the form

    valid daily-at-3am cron expression with the per-case slug embedded

    and the four axes that carry over (slug-prefix `update*`, verb

    sub-axis** on the settings/* roster, and forecasts the next case
    `API-0392 settings-updateMiddlewareTraefikConfig`.

  - `gofmt -w .` — clean (no files reformatted beyond the new entry).
  - `go mod tidy` — clean.
  - `go vet ./...` — clean.
  - `go test ./...` — all packages pass; `internal/cli` runs the
    expanded `TestAPICoverage_*` and manifest-coverage suites green
    (~1.0s wall clock).
  - `go test -race ./...` — all packages pass green under the race
    detector (~2.7s wall clock for `internal/cli`).
- **Tools NOT available locally** (documented per the verification policy):
  `goimports`, `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`, `govulncheck`,
  `goreleaser`. The repo-level `scripts/verify.sh` reports each missing
  optional tool with an install hint and never silently skips.
- **Remaining risks or follow-ups**:
  - 400 → CodeInvalidInput is technically reachable here (the inner
    schema declares `required: ["cronExpression"]`), but the harness
    reserves payload-validation failures for stories where 400 is the
    operation's *distinguishing* failure mode. A future story can add
    a focused 400-leg fixture for `updateLogCleanup` if a regression
    surfaces in payload-shape validation specific to nullable-string
    fields.
  - The `null` branch of `cronExpression`'s `anyOf` is structurally
    valid but not exercised here because the harness fixes one
    SampleBody per case. A future story whose primary coverage
    burden is nullable-string round-trip behaviour can add a
    sibling fixture under a new StoryID.
  - The trailing-comment cron-expression slug embedding
    (`"0 3 * * * # set-cov-updateLogCleanup-0391"`) relies on the
    Dokploy server tolerating cron-grammar comments (most
    standard cron parsers do; the Go `robfig/cron` library
    accepts `#`-prefixed comments). The harness only asserts
    that the request reached the server and returned 200 — it
    does not assert that the server semantically validated the
    cron string.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **`anyOf: [{type: "X"}, {type: "null"}]` is JSON-Schema's
    nullability idiom, not a polymorphic union.** When you encounter
    this shape on a Dokploy property, treat it as "type X, but null
    is also accepted" rather than "either an X or some other unknown
    shape." Both `null` and any X-typed value are structurally
    valid; the choice between them is a coverage decision, not a
    structural one. Document the choice in the case comment so a
    future contributor adding a sibling story knows which branch
    is already exercised.
  - **When the lone inner property is a domain-specific
    semi-structured string (cron expression, IP address, URL,
    regex), embedding the per-case slug as a raw bareword is
    semantically misleading.** Prefer a syntactically valid value
    of the field's grammar with the slug embedded as a comment or
    trailing identifier (here: the `# slug` comment fragment on a
    valid cron expression). This preserves both the
    fixture-isolation convention and the field's semantics on the
    wire.
  - **Slug-prefix continuity does not imply axis continuity.**
    API-0390 and API-0391 are both `update*` peers in the same
    sub-roster, but three of their seven primary axes pivot
    (inner-property-count, inner-property-type, inner-property-name).
    The slug-prefix-is-not-shape rule reasserted at API-0371..API-0390
    holds at API-0391: per-operation re-verification against
    `internal/api/data/openapi.json` is mandatory before assuming
    any field carries over from a slug-adjacent peer.
  - **The `anyOf` nullability shape is *not* a 400-distinguishing
    payload-validation case.** A 400-leg fixture remains reserved
    for stories whose coverage burden hinges on multi-field
    cross-validation, conditional `oneOf`/`anyOf` *between distinct
    shapes* (not between a scalar and its null sentinel), or
    length-bounded strings. A simple nullable-string field falls
    under the routine settings/* coverage cohort where 401 →
    CodeAuth is the canonical representative failure.

- **Remaining risks or follow-ups**: none for this

  hand-off comment for API-0394
  `settings-updateServerIp` — per the slug-prefix-is-
  not-shape rule and the cautionary precedent of the
  API-0392 → API-0393 outer-body pivot, the next
  contributor must inspect the spec directly rather
  than trusting the PRD's `requestBody.required = false`
  flag (which is ambiguous between "no body at all"
  and "body declared but optional with non-empty inner
  schema").
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **The PRD's `requestBody.required` flag is an
    insufficient proxy for the spec's outer-body shape.**
    The PRD records `requestBody.required: false,
    contentTypes: []` for API-0393, which is
    superficially compatible with two structurally
    distinct shapes: (a) no `requestBody` field at all
    in the spec (this entry's case), and (b)
    `requestBody` declared with `required: false` and
    a non-empty inner schema. Only direct inspection
    of `internal/api/data/openapi.json` settles which
    branch applies. The API-0392 hand-off comment's
    forecast that API-0393 would carry
    `requestBody.required = true` was a clean miss in
    the *opposite* direction (forecasting REQUIRED but
    the spec has ABSENT) — the correct mental model is
    that the PRD's `requestBody.required` flag tells
    you *nothing* about whether the spec declares a
    `requestBody` field; it only tells you the
    `requestBody.required` flag's value if the field
    exists. Future contributors must inspect the spec
    *unconditionally* before assuming any outer-body
    shape.
  - **The slug-prefix-is-not-shape rule extends to the
    outer-body axis.** Prior `update*` peers in
    settings/* (API-0390 `updateDockerCleanup`, API-0391
    `updateLogCleanup`, API-0392
    `updateMiddlewareTraefikConfig`) all carry a
    REQUIRED `requestBody` with at least one inner
    property. API-0393 `updateServer` shares the
    `update*` slug prefix but has no `requestBody` at
    all. This is the **first instance of an outer-body
    axis pivot inside a contiguous slug sub-roster**
    on the settings/* tag — prior pivots stayed within
    the inner-property axes (count, type, name,
    required-ness) while keeping the outer body
    REQUIRED. The lesson is that *no* axis is
    structurally privileged: any axis can pivot at any
    boundary, and per-operation re-verification is
    mandatory regardless of slug-prefix continuity.
  - **The no-body POST cohort within settings/* now
    totals seven entries** (API-0354, 0357, 0358, 0359,
    0370, 0383, 0393), spread across four slug prefixes
    (`clean*`, `getUpdateData`, `reload*`, `update*`).
    The cohort is structurally homogeneous: no body, no
    parameters, no 404, success schema `{}` with
    `additionalProperties: false`. This is the largest
    structural sub-cohort on the settings/* tag — and
    the only one that spans four distinct slug prefixes.
    Its growth pattern (one new member every 3-13
    stories) suggests future settings/* `update*` peers
    will likely add to it, but the API-0392 → API-0393
    pivot proves that within-cohort membership is *not*
    predictable from slug prefix.
  - **For no-body POSTs, omit both `SampleBody` and
    `SuccessResponse`** — the harness's
    `if len(tc.SampleBody) > 0` guard inside
    `runAPICoverageSuccess` correctly skips writing a
    request body when `SampleBody` is unset, and
    `SuccessResponse`'s default of `{}` matches the
    canonical settings/* mutating-POST 200 schema.
    Carrying an empty `SampleBody: json.RawMessage(\`{}\`)`
    would silently encode a non-empty request body on
    the wire (the JSON object `{}`) which is
    structurally distinct from a true bodyless POST.
    The API-0383 entry's "Leaving `SuccessResponse`
    unset lets the harness default to `{}`" comment is
    the canonical precedent — follow it for every
    no-body POST going forward.
  - **400 → CodeInvalidInput is structurally
    unavailable for the no-body POST cohort.** Without
    a payload to mis-shape, the operation cannot fail
    server-side payload-shape validation; the spec's
    400 response is reserved for other categories of
    invalid input (e.g. invalid `Authorization` header
    formatting) which the harness does not exercise.
    401 → CodeAuth via the harness default is therefore
    the **only** meaningful representative failure for
    no-body POST entries — there is no story-specific
    coverage burden that would justify overriding
    `FailureStatus` / `FailureCode` to 400.
  - **The body-axis flip-flop within settings/* is now
    eleven entries deep across API-0383..API-0393.**
    The body axis is the most volatile axis on the tag
    — it has flipped at every boundary in this stretch:
    no-body / required-body+inner-required (API-0386) /
    required-body+inner-optional-string-only (API-0387) /
    required-body+inner-optional-mixed (API-0388) /
    required-body+inner-required-boolean (API-0389) /
    required-body+inner-required-mixed (API-0390) /
    required-body+inner-required-nullable-string
    (API-0391) / required-body+inner-required-plain-
    string (API-0392) / no-body (API-0393). Future
    contributors should expect continued body-axis
    volatility within settings/* and per-operation
    re-verification stays mandatory across every
    family transition.

    outer-body axis oscillates.** API-0390 (REQ) →
    API-0391 (REQ) → API-0392 (REQ) → API-0393
    (ABSENT) → API-0394 (REQ). This is the first
    documented two-step oscillation within the same
    tag's slug-stem sub-roster. The slug-prefix-is-
    not-shape rule extends to the slug-stem axis:
    even matching `updateServer*` (API-0393 vs
    API-0394) does not pre-determine the outer-body
    axis. The lesson generalises: PRD
    `requestBody.required` is only one of three
    possible outer-body states (REQUIRED / OPTIONAL /
    ABSENT), and only direct inspection of
    `internal/api/data/openapi.json` settles the
    distinction between OPTIONAL (declared with
    `required: false`) and ABSENT (no `requestBody`
    field at all).
  - **Slug-on-the-wire convention scales to plausibly-
    typed string fields.** The `serverIp` field is
    conventionally an IP-address-shaped string but
    the spec declares no `format: ipv4`, no
    `pattern`, and no `examples`, so any non-empty
    string is structurally valid. Embedding the slug
    as the whole value (`"set-cov-updateServerIp-0394"`)
    rather than as a comment fragment on a
    domain-typed value (e.g., `"127.0.0.1
    # set-cov-updateServerIp-0394"` would be invalid
    because comments are not part of JSON) preserves
    the slug-on-the-wire convention without
    introducing dialect-specific syntax. The
    Dokploy server is free to either accept the
    string (the spec contract this fixture
    exercises) or reject it on IP-format grounds (a
    server-side concern outside the spec's
    declarative shape) — the harness only asserts
    spec-level structural validity.
  - **Forty-fourth entry on the settings/* roster
    keeps the per-tag-isolation rule.** No
    back-references to closed `srv-cov-*`,
    `proj-cov-*`, `org-cov-*`, `compose-cov-*`,
    `app-cov-*`, `ai-cov-*`, or any other prior
    tag's namespace — the per-tag isolation rule
    reasserted at API-0335..API-0393 holds. Each
    new settings/* entry uses
    `set-cov-<slug>-<storyID>` and is unique within
    the tag.

  within the settings/* `update*` sub-roster, but the

  forbids assuming any axis carries over even when the slug stem
  matches at `Traefik`.
- **Learnings for future iterations**:
  - **The structural-twin streak on the settings/* `update*`
    sub-roster ends at three.** API-0392 / API-0394 / API-0395
    were structurally identical "single REQUIRED plain string"
    shapes (zero-pivot triplet separated only by the API-0393
    ABSENT-body intermezzo). API-0396 breaks the streak with two
    REQUIRED + one OPTIONAL plain strings — confirming that even
    a stable triplet within a single tag's slug-prefix sub-roster
    cannot pre-determine the next entry's inner shape. The
    forward-reference lesson reasserted at API-0345..API-0395
    becomes sharper here: API-0395's hand-off comment
    explicitly forecast a possible `path` + `content` shape and
    the spec confirmed the forecast at the inner-property-count
    axis (one → three) and the inner-required-field axis (one →
    two), even while the verb, outer-body, parameter,
    response-set, and 200-shape axes stayed identical.
  - **First multi-required-field `update*` shape on settings/*.**
    Prior multi-required-field precedent within the settings/*
    tag was API-0386 `settings-saveSSHPrivateKey`
    (`name`/`privateKey` REQUIRED), but that entry sat on the
    `save*` slug-prefix sub-roster, not `update*`. API-0396 is
    the first `update*` peer requiring more than one inner
    field — useful future signal that the `update*` sub-roster's
    inner-required-field axis is **non-monotonic** (single-field
    at API-0390/0391/0392/0394/0395, multi-field at 0396), so
    no `update*`-prefix-wide invariant can be claimed.
  - **`serverId`-as-OPTIONAL is a settings/* convention worth
    flagging.** API-0394 `settings-updateServerIp`'s `serverId`
    was the entire payload (REQUIRED in that op's local
    semantics), whereas API-0396 declares `serverId` OPTIONAL
    alongside two REQUIRED file-mutation fields. The Dokploy
    convention surfacing here: when `serverId` accompanies
    OTHER REQUIRED fields, it scopes the operation to a remote
    Dokploy worker server (and absent → local Dokploy server);
    when `serverId` IS the operation (e.g. `updateServerIp`),
    its presence/required-status flips. Future settings/*
    entries with multi-field shapes carrying `serverId` should
    inherit this convention check.
  - **Path-shaped string fixture choice.** The spec declares
    `path` as a plain string with no `format`, `pattern`, or
    `examples`, so any non-empty string is structurally valid.
    Embedding the slug as the **basename** of an absolute
    filesystem path (e.g.
    `/etc/dokploy/traefik/set-cov-updateTraefikFile-0396.yml`)
    rather than as a comment fragment preserves the
    slug-on-the-wire convention without contaminating the field's
    conventional semantics. Mirrors the API-0394 `serverIp`
    fixture choice (slug-as-whole-string) where the field's
    conventional shape did not admit an in-band comment syntax.
  - **OPTIONAL-field omission as deliberate coverage choice.**
    This is the first entry on the settings/* roster where the
    inner schema has both REQUIRED and OPTIONAL plain-string
    fields. The fixture deliberately omits the OPTIONAL
    `serverId` so the success-leg exercise stays focused on the
    structurally-minimal valid payload (REQUIRED fields populated,
    OPTIONAL fields absent). Populating the OPTIONAL field would
    have shifted the fixture toward an orthogonal "scoped to
    remote worker" code path which is not part of this story's
    acceptance criteria. Future stories with OPTIONAL fields
    should adopt the same default unless the OPTIONAL field is
    the operation's *distinguishing* coverage axis.

    versus the prior settings/* `update*` peer: the body is
    `{additionalPorts: [{targetPort:number, publishedPort:number,
    protocol: "tcp"|"udp"|"sctp"}], serverId?: string}` — the **first
    array-of-objects body field on the entire settings/* roster** and
    the first non-string outer-property-type pivot within the
    settings/* `update*` sub-roster. `additionalPorts` REQUIRED;
    `serverId` OPTIONAL. The fixture provides a structurally-minimal

  - `gofmt -w .` — clean.

  representative-failure assertions all green for
  `settings-updateTraefikPorts` via the existing `TestAPICoverage_*`
  harness. `expectedOperationCount = 450` in
  `internal/api/registry_test.go` already includes this op (the
  count is locked against the embedded openapi.json, not the
  coverage test).
- Remaining risks or follow-ups:
  - The settings/* `update*` sub-roster continues at API-0398
    `settings-updateWebServerTraefikConfig` (POST with required body).
    Per the slug-prefix-is-not-shape lesson reasserted at
    API-0371..API-0397, sharing the `update*` slug prefix and the
    `Traefik` slug-stem with API-0392/API-0395/API-0396/API-0397 does
    NOT pre-determine the inner-property-count, inner-property-type,
    or inner-required-field axes — the next contributor MUST
    re-verify against `internal/api/data/openapi.json >
    /settings.updateWebServerTraefikConfig > post` before assuming
    any field carries over. `updateWebServerTraefikConfig` may declare
    a single-string-content shape (matching API-0395
    `updateTraefikConfig`), a multi-string shape (matching API-0396
    `updateTraefikFile`), an array-of-objects shape (matching this
    entry), or an entirely orthogonal shape.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **Array-of-objects body fields are coverage-axis-distinct from
    scalar-only bodies.** The fixture exercises the inner-item schema
    by populating one fully-formed item (every REQUIRED inner-inner
    field set, no OPTIONAL ones). Multi-element arrays would shift
    coverage toward an orthogonal "multi-port-mapping" axis that is
    not part of the per-operation acceptance criteria.
  - **Slug-on-the-wire convention does NOT apply to numeric or
    enum-bounded fields.** The `set-cov-updateTraefikPorts-0397`
    fixture-token base is established for namespace tracking but
    cannot be embedded in the body anywhere because every inner-inner
    field is `number` or `string`-enum-constrained. The convention
    only applies to free-form string fields (cf. the precedent across
    API-0386/API-0387/API-0388/API-0390/API-0391/API-0392/API-0394/
    API-0395/API-0396 where `path`-shaped or YAML-content-shaped
    free-form strings carry the slug).
  - **Enum-constrained string fields must take a value from the enum
    list.** The `protocol` field's `enum: ["tcp", "udp", "sctp"]`
    means the fixture must pick one of those literal values; using a
    slug-embedded string like `set-cov-updateTraefikPorts-0397` would
    fail enum validation server-side.
  - **`number`-typed fields accept integers in JSON.** Both
    `targetPort` and `publishedPort` are typed `number` (not
    `integer`) in the spec, and JSON-RFC-8259 number literals like
    `8443` parse cleanly into either. The fixture uses bare integers
    rather than fractional notation to match the conventional port-
    number on-the-wire shape.
  - **Body-axis flip-flop now fifteen entries deep within settings/*.**
    The continuous flip-flop across API-0383..API-0397 reaffirms that
    per-operation re-verification is mandatory across every family
    transition; no body-axis assumption can be safely inherited even
    within a single tag.

  API-0351 and extended through API-0397. Per-case fixture token
  `set-cov-updateWebServerTraefikConfig-0398` is unique within the

  but stays on the `Traefik` slug-stem; per the slug-stem-is-not-
  shape lesson it may declare a single-string shape (matching this
  entry / API-0395), a multi-string shape (matching API-0396), an

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **Shape-collision with a prior peer is a permitted outcome, not
    a violation of slug-stem-is-not-shape.** API-0398 collides with
    API-0395 on every shape-defining axis because the spec authors
    chose to use the same single-string body for both Traefik
    config update operations (one for the edge router, one for the
    web server). The slug-stem-is-not-shape rule says the
    contributor cannot ASSUME shape inheritance; it does not say
    the spec cannot DECLARE shape collision. The contributor still
    re-verifies the spec; if collision occurs, the `// Forward-
    reference confirmation` comment names the colliding peer
    explicitly and lists the matching axes so the next reader can
    diff cleanly.

    suspension.** API-0397's body had only numeric and enum-bounded
    inner fields, so the slug could not be embedded. API-0398's
    single free-form string field restores the convention. Future
    peers should expect the convention to apply field-by-field
    based on type, not entry-by-entry.
  - **No OPTIONAL outer fields → no carve-out comment needed.**
    Unlike API-0396/API-0397 which both carry an OPTIONAL `serverId`
    and required a "deliberately omitted" carve-out, API-0398 has
    only the single REQUIRED `traefikConfig` field. The
    structurally-minimal valid body and the maximal valid body are
    identical, so the fixture-conventions section is shorter by one
    bullet.
  - **Body-axis flip-flop now sixteen entries deep within
    settings/*.** The continuous flip-flop across API-0383..API-0398
    reaffirms that per-operation re-verification is mandatory; the
    shape-collision with API-0395 is the first repeat-shape entry in
    the settings/* `update*` sub-roster but does NOT establish a
    pattern — the next entry (API-0399 `writeTraefikEnv`) must still
    be re-verified per the slug-prefix-is-not-shape rule.

    REQUIRED, the fixture populates only those required fields and leaves
    every optional knob unset. This keeps the success-leg assertion
    focused on the required-field forwarding contract and avoids
    accidentally codifying the optional-field default behaviour as
    contract.
  - `metadata` declared as `type: object` with no `properties` is a
    free-form bag — any JSON object structurally satisfies the contract.
    The fixture supplies a single-key object whose value carries the
    same per-case sentinel so the slug-on-the-wire token base remains
    traceable across every populated string surface.
  - The slug-prefix-is-not-shape lesson holds even within the same tag:
    among user/* alone we now have a parameter-free GET (API-0427), a
    fully-required-body POST (API-0428), a single-required-query GET
    (API-0429), and a partially-required-body POST (API-0430) — four
    orthogonal shape signatures sharing the `user-` operation-stem.
    Future user/* contributors must continue per-operation re-verification.
  - **404-absence cluster within user/* POSTs.** Both API-0428
    `user-assignPermissions` and API-0430 `user-createApiKey` declare
    response codes 200/400/401/403/500 with no 404. The structural
    rationale is the same: neither operation performs a by-id lookup
    before its write (assignPermissions scopes by body's `id` rather
    than path; createApiKey mints a fresh resource), so CodeNotFound is
    not an applicable failure representative for either entry.

    Leaving SamplePathParams and SampleBody unset is the correct
    minimal envelope; `buildCoverageInputArgs` writes only the present
    fields, and `runAPICoverageSuccess` re-reads `r.URL.Query()` to
    confirm propagation. Anything else would conflate the contract.

- **Parameter-free POSTs are a real shape category.** Prior user/*
  POSTs all carried request bodies (API-0428/0430/0431). API-0432 is

  entirely and declares zero parameters. The harness handles this case

  exercises the same code branch.
- **400 → CodeInvalidInput is structurally unreachable when the spec
  declares zero input axes.** Even though the spec lists 400 in the
  response set, with no parameters and no request body the CLI cannot
  construct a syntactically invalid payload. Recording this as an

  most informative representative because authentication is the
  universal failure mode every authenticated POST must re-prove.
- **Cross-roster precedent for parameter-free POSTs is rare.** Most
  prior parameter-free coverage stories were GETs (API-0006 `ai-getAll`,
  API-0051 `bitbucket-bitbucketProviders`, API-0427 `user-all`). When
  modelling future parameter-free POSTs, lean on the API-0432 entry
  for the body-shape narrative rather than on those GET openers — the
  GET cases share the no-fixture pattern but differ on the verb and
  on the harness's body-assertion gate.
- **The forward-reference comment in API-0427 already enumerates
  API-0428..API-0436 by name** including API-0432 `user-generateToken`,
  API-0433 `user-get`, API-0434 `user-getBackups`, etc. Future user/*
  iterations can confirm the next slug at a glance without re-reading
  the PRD index — but the spec axes (parameters, body, responses) must
  always be re-verified per-operation as the slug-stem-is-not-shape
  lesson dictates.

  `docker-getContainers`).

  - None for this story. The next priority-3 docker/* peer is API-0109
    `docker-getContainers` — per the slug-prefix-is-not-shape lesson the next
    contributor must re-verify the spec at
    `internal/api/data/openapi.json > /docker.getContainers > get` rather than
    assume it inherits this entry's REQUIRED+OPTIONAL shape (per spec scan
    API-0109 has only an optional `serverId` and no REQUIRED parameter, so it
    represents a different sub-shape).
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **Per-tag opener fixture-isolation namespace.** Every first entry in a new
    tag opens a fresh `<tag>-cov-*` namespace. The destination/* tag closed at
    API-0107; API-0108 opens `docker-cov-*`. The closed namespaces (now
    explicitly enumerated in the entry's "must not back-reference" list) are
    `admin-cov-*`, `ai-cov-*`, `app-cov-*`, `backup-cov-*`, `bb-cov-*`,
    `cert-cov-*`, `clu-cov-*`, `compose-cov-*`, `deployment-cov-*`,
    `dest-cov-*`, `org-cov-*`, `proj-cov-*`, `set-cov-*`, `srv-cov-*`. Future
    docker/* peers (API-0109..API-0114) must stay inside `docker-cov-*` and
    add no cross-tag value-axis literals other than the established
    `server-cov-*` (optional `serverId`) and `dst-cov-*` (backup
    `destinationId`) precedents.
  - **REQUIRED + OPTIONAL GET shape precedent.** The closest cross-tag template
    for `docker-getConfig` is API-0077 `compose-getTags` (REQUIRED + OPTIONAL,
    two params) and API-0041 `backup-listBackupFiles` (REQUIRED + REQUIRED +
    OPTIONAL, three params). Both populate the optional axis so the success-leg
    `r.URL.Query()` re-read exercises every declared parameter — the harness
    does not gate on `required`-ness and forwards whatever `SampleQuery`
    carries. Future API-0109..API-0113 docker/* GETs that share this REQUIRED
    + OPTIONAL pattern can copy the API-0108 docstring template verbatim and
    swap the StoryID, slug, parameter names, and per-operation cross-references.
  - **Per-tag opener default failure leg stays at 401 → CodeAuth.** Even though
    `docker.getConfig` declares 404 in its response set (an unresolvable
    `containerId`), the kickoff entry for a new tag exercises the universal
    `E_AUTH` invariant — auth is the single failure mode every authenticated
    Dokploy operation must re-prove before path/row resolution runs. The
    404 → CodeNotFound representative is reserved for a later docker/* peer
    where the spec re-verification confirms 404 is exercisable from a
    legitimate `--input` document. This precedent now holds across every
    per-tag opener (API-0006 ai, API-0021 application, API-0094 deployment,
    API-0246 organization, API-0427 user, API-0108 docker).
  - **Forward-reference comment for the next case is mandatory.** Every entry
    closes with a reminder of the next per-tag PRD slug AND the slug-prefix-is-
    not-shape lesson. API-0109 `docker-getContainers` is the natural next
    docker/* coverage story; its spec lookup is a hard gate before any
    contributor can copy this entry's shape.

## 2026-05-08 — API-0440 Cover user-haveRootAccess (GET /user.haveRootAccess)

  StoryID order after API-0439 `user-getUserByToken`.
- Spec re-verified against
  `internal/api/data/openapi.json > /user.haveRootAccess > get`:
  GET, no `requestBody`, **zero** declared parameters
  (no query, no path, no header). 200 schema is `{}` with
  `additionalProperties: false`. Failure cohort 400/401/403/404/500.
- Wire shape: parameter-free GET. Mirrors the same precedent as
  API-0427 `user-all`, API-0433 `user-get`, API-0434 `user-getBackups`,
  API-0436 `user-getInvitations`, API-0437 `user-getMetricsToken`,
  API-0438 `user-getServerMetrics`. SampleBody/SampleQuery/
  SamplePathParams all left zero so the success-leg subtest reduces to
  the wire-level invariants — `runAPICoverageSuccess`'s
  `len(tc.SampleBody) > 0` gate (and the SampleQuery/SamplePathParams
  guards) short-circuit the body assertion when none of those three
  is populated.
- Failure-leg fields intentionally omitted:
    * **404 → CodeNotFound is structurally inapplicable** — the
      operation accepts no resource identifier, so no `--input`
      payload can surface a missing resource.
    * **400 → CodeInvalidInput is unavailable** — zero parameters and
      no body means no payload can be syntactically invalid.
    * 401 → CodeAuth via the harness defaults
      (`tc.FailureStatus == 0` → 401, `tc.FailureCode == ""` →
      `yerr.CodeAuth`) is the most informative representative for an
      authenticated GET, matching every prior parameter-free user/*
      peer.
- Fixture token base `usr-cov-haveRootAccess-0440` follows the
  `<tag>-cov-<slug>-<storyID>` convention and lives only in the
  comment as the namespace anchor (no string field exists in the
  operation to embed the slug into).
- Files changed:
    * internal/cli/api_coverage_test.go (+136 lines, one struct literal
      appended)
    * ralph/prd.json (single `passes: false` → `true` flip on API-0440)
    * ralph/progress.txt (this entry)
- Verification run from repo root:
    * `gofmt -w .` — clean
    * `go mod tidy` — no changes
    * `go vet ./...` — clean
    * `go test ./... -count=1` — all packages pass
    * `go test -race ./... -count=1` — all packages pass
    * `goimports`, `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`, `govulncheck`,
      `goreleaser` — not installed locally, documented per the global
      pattern.
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
    * Next priority-2 backlog entry per the in-comment hand-off forecast
      is API-0441 `user-one` (GET `/user.one`). Per the
      slug-prefix-is-not-shape and slug-stem-is-not-shape lessons
      reasserted at API-0371..API-0439, the next contributor must
      re-verify against `internal/api/data/openapi.json` rather than
      assume any field carries over from API-0440.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
    * The append-only `coveredAPIOperations` table is by now an
      extremely well-documented per-operation fixture log: even
      shape-twin entries (parameter-free GETs in this case) restate the
      wire shape, the slug-on-the-wire status, the failure-leg
      reasoning, and the next-entry hand-off forecast in full. This is
      load-bearing for future contributors who land mid-roster and
      need to reproduce a peer's reasoning without re-reading the
      whole table.
    * **Distinguish "structurally inapplicable" 404 from
      "shape-secondary" 404.** Parameter-free GETs (API-0438,
      API-0440) cannot surface 404 via any `--input` payload — the
      operation takes no resource ID — so the 404 is a defensive
      spec declaration, full stop. Single-required-query GETs like
      API-0439 `user-getUserByToken` *can* surface 404 (an unknown
      `token` is the natural trigger), but the 404 →
      CodeNotFound representative is reserved for the canonical
      `*-one` entry within the tag (API-0433 `user-get` per the
      API-0427 hand-off forecast). Both reasons land at "401 →
      CodeAuth via harness default" but for different structural
      reasons; record which one applies in the comment so future
      contributors don't re-litigate.
    * **Re-verify the spec, do not extrapolate from the slug.**
      `getServerMetrics` / `getMetricsToken` / `getContainerMetrics`
      share the `Metrics` slug stem but carry orthogonal wire shapes
      (no params / no params / four required query params). The same
      caveat applied here: `haveRootAccess` shares no slug with prior
      peers but must still be spec-verified rather than assumed to
      carry over from API-0439 `user-getUserByToken` (which has
      a single required query param) just because the previous
      entry was the immediate predecessor in the user/* roster.

  resource keyed by id). Per the bitbucket/* precedent at

  - `go test ./...` — pass (all packages green)
  - `go test -race ./...` — pass
  - `goimports`, `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`, `govulncheck`,
    `goreleaser` — not installed locally; documented previously,
    skipped here per established practice.
- Remaining risks/follow-ups:
  - The docker/* roster's 404→CodeNotFound representative slot is
    now formally *unreserved* — the docker/* tag exposes only
    parameter-free, optional-serverId, or appName-keyed endpoints
    in priority-3 coverage, so no docker/* peer offers an
    id-bearing GET that would naturally consume the override. The
    docker/* tag may legitimately exit without a 404 representative.
  - API-0114 `docker-restartContainer` is the next docker/* case
    per PRD ordering — declared a POST per the spec preview, almost
    certainly carrying a request body shape distinct from the
    appName-keyed GETs covered to date. The next contributor must
    re-verify the spec before assuming any field carries over.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - **Forward-reference predictions are hypotheses, not contracts.**
    API-0112's design header predicted API-0113 would host the
    docker/* 404 override "if 404 exercisability is confirmed at
    spec re-verification". The re-verification here disconfirmed
    the prediction — `docker-getStackContainersByAppName` is
    structurally identical to API-0112 (appName-keyed list, not
    id-bearing). Always re-verify and be prepared to *retract* a
    prior story's forward reference. Documenting the retraction in
    the new entry's design header is the canonical way to keep the
    rationale chain auditable.
  - **Slug-prefix coincidence ≠ shape inheritance, even within a
    single tag.** API-0112 (`getServiceContainers*`) and API-0113
    (`getStackContainers*`) happen to share an exact wire shape
    (REQUIRED appName + OPTIONAL serverId, empty 200), but that
    coincidence was confirmed by direct OpenAPI inspection — not
    inherited from the peer entry. The slug-prefix-is-not-shape
    lesson re-asserted at API-0345..API-0440 applies even to
    near-duplicate operation names within the same tag prefix.
  - **404 override slot can legitimately exit a tag empty.** Not
    every tag *must* consume the 404→CodeNotFound representative.
    If a tag's roster contains no canonical by-id GET (only
    parameter-free, optional-serverId, or list-style endpoints),
    the 404 slot stays unused and the tag closes on the
    harness-default 401→CodeAuth path. The docker/* roster is
    on track to be such a tag.

    slug-stem-is-not-shape lessons within a single tag — even with
    a shared `user-` operation-stem and shared POST method, no axis
    from API-0442's single-string body carries over.

    When a body declares two or more REQUIRED free-form strings, each
    field gets its own per-field suffix appended to the
    `<tag>-cov-<slug>-<storyID>` base so the success-leg body
    assertion in `runAPICoverageSuccess` can independently trace each
    field's propagation through the `--input` JSON `body` field. The
    suffix reuses the field name's first three letters (`-inv`,
    `-not`) — mnemonic but compact, and orthogonal across fields
    within one entry.

    user/* tag, this is the canonical home for the two-required-

    forward-reference-is-hypothesis lesson reasserted at API-0113,
    every such reference must be re-verified against the spec before
    assuming axis inheritance.

    retrievals.** Within the user/* roster API-0441 `user-one`
    remains the only 404-override entry; API-0442 `user-remove` and
    API-0443 `user-sendInvitation` both fall back to the harness
    default 401 → CodeAuth because the spec funnels their by-id
    resolution failures into 400/403. The 404-override is reserved
    for canonical by-id retrievals (`*-one`, `*-get`), not for
    destructive or effectful mutations whose body fields name the
    target resource.

- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - The user/* tag's priority-2 backlog is now fully covered through
    API-0444. The next PRD-ordered entry drops to **priority 3** and
    crosses tag boundaries to API-0114 `docker-restartContainer`
    (POST /docker.restartContainer). Per the forward-reference lesson
    the next contributor must re-verify against
    `internal/api/data/openapi.json > /docker.restartContainer > post`
    before assuming any axis carries over from this entry — neither
    tag, operation-stem, nor request-body shape is shared, so no axis
    inheritance applies. Most candidate docker/* POSTs are container-
    keyed mutations that typically declare a small body referencing a
    specific container by id; that prediction is a hypothesis, not a
    contract, and must be confirmed at re-verification.
  - The user/* roster's 404-override slot was last consumed at
    API-0441 `user-one` and is now formally closed for this tag
    (every remaining user/* operation in priority-2 was a mutation
    whose spec does not declare 404). The 404 → CodeNotFound
    representative slot for the user/* tag is locked in at the
    canonical by-id retrieval (`*-one`), as predicted.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **All-optional body POST shape — first such on user/* roster.**
    The user/* roster's eighteenth entry introduces a body shape
    distinct from every prior covered peer: zero REQUIRED fields,
    23 declared OPTIONAL properties, including seven nullable
    `anyOf [T, null]` shapes. This is the conventional signature
    of `*-update` mutations whose REST-over-RPC surface lets a
    client mutate any subset of an existing row's columns. The
    design implication: the success-path fixture should populate
    a *representative subset* (one or two strings, one boolean,
    one number) rather than attempt exhaustive field enumeration.
    The harness contract is one representative success path; field
    enumeration belongs to a hypothetical schema-validator-driven
    fuzz suite, not the per-story contract test.
  - **`required: null` vs. `required: []` are equivalent at the
    spec level.** The `/user.update > post` body schema omits the
    `required` key entirely; `jq` returns `null`. Both shapes mean
    "all fields optional" and the harness's body-byte assertion
    treats them identically — no `required` field needs to appear
    in the SampleBody at all.
  - **Nullable `anyOf [T, null]` shapes ≠ T-or-omitted.** The seven
    nullable fields in the body schema declare an explicit
    `null`-or-T union. Omitting the field entirely (the conventional
    interpretation of "optional") is *also* valid because the field
    is not in `required`, so the success-path fixture sidesteps the
    union shape by simply not populating those fields. Future
    coverage where a nullable field is the operation's
    *uniquely distinguishing* axis must populate the field with an
    explicit JSON `null` to exercise the union — but a generic
    success path has no obligation to do so.
  - **Forward-reference predictions are hypotheses, not contracts
    — reasserted.** API-0443's design header predicted that
    API-0444's `*-update` shape would be a "many-field partial-
    update body shape distinct from this two-string body's
    signature". The re-verification here *confirmed* that
    prediction — but the confirmation was independent of the
    forward-reference; the shape was rederived from
    `/user.update > post` directly, not inherited from API-0443's
    hypothesis. The slug-prefix-is-not-shape lesson stands: every
    new entry must re-verify against the OpenAPI document.
  - **Priority-2 backlog closing — tag-boundary transition ahead.**
    API-0444 closes out the user/* tag's priority-2 contributions.
    The next PRD-ordered story (API-0114 `docker-restartContainer`)
    is priority 3 and on a different tag. Cross-tag transitions
    re-set every axis hypothesis: the docker/* fixture-isolation
    namespace was established at earlier docker/* entries
    (priority-3 cases reaching back to API-0001), and any
    docker/*-specific conventions (slug prefix, harness fixture
    patterns) belong to that tag, not to user/*.

    `<tag>-create` mutation cohort.
  - For POST cases with a required body, supply ONLY the
    REQUIRED schema properties in `SampleBody`. The harness
    asserts byte-for-byte body propagation, so optional fields
    add fixture noise without strengthening the assertion. Use
    the `<tag>-cov-<slug>-<storyID>` token convention so `git
    grep` can trace any fixture string back to its PRD story.
  - The `runAPICoverageSuccess` helper round-trips both `got` and
    `want` through `json.Unmarshal`/`Marshal` before comparing,
    so multi-line backtick-quoted JSON in `SampleBody` is safe;
    no need to minify the fixture string by hand.

  - Added a registry-driven coverage case for the Dokploy

    lesson against `internal/api/data/openapi.json >
    /domain.delete > post`: a **POST** with **no parameters** and
    a **REQUIRED request body** whose schema is the closed-shape
    single-string-scalar `{domainId}` (required, no optionals).
    Responses 200/400/401/403/500 — the spec does **not** declare

    `runAPICoverageSuccess` activates the JSON content-type and
    byte-for-byte body comparison legs; the fixture supplies the

    propagated the body verbatim.

  - The "highest priority" PRD ordering uses LOWER number = HIGHER
    priority (priority 1, 2 fully done; priority 3 has 20 remaining and
    is the current head; priority 4 and 5 are deeper backlog). Do not
    sort descending by priority value — that picks priority-5 work
    while priority-3 is open.
  - mounts/* is the second per-tag roster (after environment/*) on
    the priority-3 backlog. The mounts-cov-* fixture namespace was
    opened by API-0188 and continues here; mountains of closed
    namespaces (admin/ai/app/backup/bb/cert/clu/compose/deployment/
    dest/docker/domain/environment/org/proj/set/srv/usr-cov-*) must be
    listed in the comment block per the per-tag isolation rule.
  - Three-required-field mixed-type body shape (string-enum + two
    plain strings) is a NEW shape on the covered-POST roster — prior
    POST cohort was either two-required-string (API-0118/0122/0125)
    or single-required-string (API-0249). The harness's byte-level
    body assertion treats enums as plain strings on the wire, so no

    `internal/api/data/openapi.json` before assuming any field shape (per the
    forward-reference lesson re-stated on every recent mounts/* entry).
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The `coveredAPIOperations` slice is "sorted by StoryID for diff-friendliness"
    but the PRD is consumed in `sort_by(.priority, .id)` order, so the slice has
    visible gaps (e.g. API-0130 → API-0188 → API-0193 → API-0246). Insert the
    new case literal at its StoryID-sorted position even when that splits an
    existing range — the harness loops the slice in declaration order, not by
    StoryID.
  - `jq '[.userStories[] | select(.passes == false)] | sort_by(.priority, .id)
    | .[0]'` is the canonical query for "next failing story". Picking by
    `.id` alone (or the first `passes == false` in document order) can
    silently jump priority tiers — that's how this iteration first nearly
    picked API-0131 (priority 5) when API-0193 (priority 3) was still open.
  - Update-by-id mutations (`*-update`) in Dokploy follow a stable two-axis
    template: closed-shape `{<entity>Id}` body + 401→CodeAuth failure leg +
    empty `{}` success. API-0122 `domain-update`, API-0130 `environment-update`,
    and API-0193 `mounts-update` are the canonical exemplars; future `*-update`
    stories should copy this shape and only deviate when the spec demands.
  - Optional-field enumeration in the spec mixes `anyOf [string, null]`
    (nullable string) with non-nullable enums and plain strings; *all* are
    optional unless listed in the schema's `required` array. Don't treat a
    non-nullable enum as required just because it has no `null` branch — the
    `required` array is the only source of truth.
  - Verification baseline confirmed unchanged: `gofmt -w .`, `go mod tidy`,
    `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./...` all pass on this
    iteration without any source-file change outside the appended case
    literal. The harness genuinely scales to one struct literal per story.

    `internal/api/data/openapi.json > /swarm.getNodeInfo > get` and

    the forward-reference lesson reasserted at API-0345..API-0444 —
    even the shared `swarm-getNode` operation-stem does not pre-

    All three swarm/* fixtures should stay on harness-default 401 →
    CodeAuth unless one of them surfaces payload validation as a
    *uniquely distinguishing* failure mode (none does at present).
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **Tag-roster opener with no canonical `*-one` peer.** When a
    tag roster contains no by-id resource lookup (every operation in
    the tag is a list/probe/effect rather than a primary-key fetch),
    the per-tag opener convention's reservation of 404 →
    CodeNotFound for `*-one` peers becomes shape-inapplicable to the
    entire roster. The swarm/* tag is the first such roster
    encountered (three GETs, all listing-shaped, all scoped only by
    an OPTIONAL `serverId`) — every entry stays on harness-default
    401 → CodeAuth without any 404 override anywhere in the
    roster. Future tag rosters whose every operation is a
    listing/probe (rather than a by-id mix) should follow the same
    pattern: harness-default 401 → CodeAuth across the whole
    roster, no 404 override at any entry.
  - **OPTIONAL single-only-param GET shape — the OPTIONAL/REQUIRED
    distinction matters at the per-case level.** API-0429
    `user-checkUserOrganizations` and API-0423 `swarm-getNodeApps`
    are both single-query-param GETs but differ on the OPTIONAL-vs-
    REQUIRED axis: API-0429's REQUIRED `userId` would 400 if
    omitted; API-0423's OPTIONAL `serverId` is a scoping
    discriminator that may be omitted entirely (the spec then
    returns the global view). Both populate the param with the
    slug-on-the-wire sentinel so the success-leg query assertion
    exercises the populated branch — but the *meaning* of populating
    differs: REQUIRED-branch fixtures verify the only valid input
    shape, while OPTIONAL-branch fixtures opt into the worker-
    scoped execution path the spec authorises but does not require.
    Future contributors must re-verify each spec's `required` flag
    per-parameter (the OpenAPI default when omitted is `false`,
    which makes single-param GETs ambiguous at first glance).
  - **PRD priority transition crossings are explicit, not implicit.**
    When the PRD-ordered backlog rolls from one priority class to
    another, the new opener's comment should explicitly call out
    the transition ("priority-2 user/* roster closed at API-0444,
    priority-3 swarm/* roster opens here") so future contributors
    reading the file in StoryID order understand the cross-priority
    insertion. Don't conflate StoryID order (file-diff stability)
    with PRD priority order (commit-sequence chronology) — the two
    are decoupled.
  - **Predecessor "next case" forecasts age into history.** API-0399
    forecasts API-0427; API-0444 forecasts API-0114. Both were
    accurate at their respective commit times but now read as
    historical because the forecasted next-stories have since
    shipped. The convention is to NOT back-edit historical
    forecasts — the new entry's own comment carries the
    *current-truth* forecast for the *next* pending case
    (API-0423's tail forecasts API-0424).
  - **`swarm-cov-*` is now an established per-tag namespace.** The
    next two swarm/* contributors (API-0424, API-0425) must use
    `swarm-cov-getNodeInfo-0424` / `swarm-cov-getNodes-0425` as
    their fixture token bases per the per-tag isolation rule
    reasserted across every prior tag's namespace.

    `mariadb-changeStatus` has zero optional fields. The fixture
    is necessarily exhaustive in REQUIRED scope and trivially
    minimal in OPTIONAL scope. When opening a tag whose payloads
    are zero-optional, this can be called out explicitly in the
    case comment so a future credential-redaction audit reads the
    coincidence as a property of the spec, not an unsafe shortcut.
  - **404 absence on status-mutations.** Status-mutation
    operations (`*-changeStatus` peers across the mariadb / mongo
    / mysql / postgres / redis / etc. tags) gate on a body-
    supplied resource id, but the Dokploy spec models the
    "missing resource" failure through 400 (validation) and 403
    (RBAC), never 404. So 404 → CodeNotFound coverage has no
    canonical home in the `*-changeStatus` failure surface, and
    the harness default 401 → CodeAuth is the most informative
    representative for this shape of operation. Opt out of the
    404 override at every entry in this cohort.
  - **Enum-value picks must be members of the declared enum.**
    `applicationStatus: "idle"` is one of four spec-declared enum
    values (`idle`/`running`/`done`/`error`). The harness only
    asserts byte-for-byte body propagation, so the choice is
    orthogonal to the contract leg, but the value MUST remain a
    member of the spec-declared enum so a future server-side
    schema validator (parallel to the registry-side
    `additionalProperties: false` invariant on the response) will
    accept the fixture.
---

## 2026-05-08 - API-0161 — Cover mariadb-create (POST /mariadb.create)
- Added mariadb-create (priority-4) to the canonical apiCoverageCase

  forward-reference left by API-0160 and continuing inside the
  `mariadb-cov-*` per-tag fixture-isolation namespace opened by that
  kickoff entry.
- Spec re-verified directly against
  `internal/api/data/openapi.json > /mariadb.create > post`:
  POST, no parameters, requestBody REQUIRED with five REQUIRED
  top-level string fields (`name`, `environmentId`, `databaseName`,
  `databaseUser`, `databasePassword`) and five OPTIONAL fields
  (`appName` (string), `dockerImage` (string, default `mariadb:6`),
  `databaseRootPassword` (string), `description` (anyOf [string, null]),
  `serverId` (anyOf [string, null])). Responses 200/400/401/403/500
  (no 404, mirroring every prior covered `*-create` mutation —
  API-0118 `domain-create`, API-0125 `environment-create`, API-0131
  `gitea-create`, API-0298 `redirects-create`, API-0331
  `security-create`). 200 = `{}` + `additionalProperties: false`.
- Fixture supplies exactly the five REQUIRED fields and nothing else.
  Per the API-0131 minimal-required-only credential-safety rule, the
  OPTIONAL `databaseRootPassword` is intentionally omitted so a future
  credential-redaction audit cannot regress on a fixture that hard-
  codes a second secret-shaped value beyond the REQUIRED
  `databasePassword` slot. The REQUIRED `databasePassword` literal
  carries the deterministic-but-clearly-fake
  `mariadb-cov-create-0161-databasePassword` token suffix for `git
  grep` traceability and unmistakable fixture-token shape.
- Failure leg: harness defaults (401 → CodeAuth). 404 →
  CodeNotFound is structurally unavailable (no 404 in spec); 400 →
  CodeInvalidInput reserved for stories where payload validation is
  the uniquely distinguishing failure mode, which a five-required-
  scalar create-mutation is not. 401 → CodeAuth pins the bearer-
  token invariant consistent with the mariadb/* kickoff at API-0160.
- Files changed:
  - `internal/cli/api_coverage_test.go` — appended apiCoverageCase
    entry between API-0160 and API-0188 (StoryID-sorted insertion)

  - `ralph/progress.txt` — this entry

  - `go mod tidy` — clean
  - `go vet ./...` — clean
  - `go test ./...` — all packages pass (internal/cli 1.359s)
  - `go test -race ./...` — all packages pass (internal/cli 2.909s);
    the new `TestAPICoverage_*` family spawned the
    `API-0161/mariadb-create` subtest across all five legs
    (RegistryInvariants, SchemaCommandWorks, ManifestListsOperation,

  - `goimports`, `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`, `govulncheck`,

  - Next case in the PRD-ordered priority-4 backlog is API-0162
    `mariadb-deploy` (declared POST in the PRD; next contributor
    must re-verify against `internal/api/data/openapi.json` per
    the forward-reference lesson before assuming any field shape).
    The `mariadb-cov-*` namespace stays open for the rest of the
    mariadb/* roster (API-0160..API-0173, fourteen operations
    per the PRD listing).
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **Five-required-scalar `*-create` body is the largest REQUIRED-
    only create-mutation fixture covered to date.** API-0118
    `domain-create`, API-0122 `domain-update`, API-0125
    `environment-create`, and API-0131 `gitea-create` each topped
    out at two REQUIRED string scalars; `mariadb-create` raises
    that ceiling to five and stresses the body-forwarding leg's
    tolerance for multi-field payloads in a way the smaller
    precedents do not. No harness change was needed — the
    `len(tc.SampleBody) > 0` gate at `runAPICoverageSuccess`
    handles arbitrary-shape bodies — but the precedent should be
    cited for any future create-mutation whose REQUIRED-field
    count exceeds five.
  - **Two credential-shaped slots in one schema, one REQUIRED + one
    OPTIONAL.** mariadb-create is the first covered operation where
    the schema declares two distinct password fields
    (`databasePassword` REQUIRED, `databaseRootPassword` OPTIONAL).
    The minimal-required-only fixture rule cleanly resolves the
    tension: the REQUIRED slot carries a deterministic-but-clearly-
    fake fixture token (still safe under the redactor because it
    is shaped `<tag>-cov-<slug>-<storyID>-<field>`), and the
    OPTIONAL slot is omitted entirely so no second secret-shaped
    value enters the test surface. Future stories whose schemas
    declare both REQUIRED and OPTIONAL credential fields should
    follow the same split.
  - **`*-create` mutations remain the canonical 401→CodeAuth-only
    failure-leg shape.** Every `*-create` operation covered to
    date (API-0118 `domain-create`, API-0125 `environment-create`,
    API-0131 `gitea-create`, API-0298 `redirects-create`, API-0331
    `security-create`, and now API-0161 `mariadb-create`) declares
    200/400/401/403/500 with **no 404** — the by-id read leg does
    not exist on a constructor — and the harness-default 401 →
    CodeAuth representative remains the most informative single
    failure mode. This pattern can now be cited as a one-line
    rationale in future `*-create` cases rather than re-justified
    from first principles.
  - **Forward-reference convention extended into the priority-4
    bucket.** API-0160's forecast of API-0161 saved a round of
    spec-discovery scanning, exactly as API-0425's forecast saved
    work for API-0160. This entry forecasts API-0162
    `mariadb-deploy` to keep the chain unbroken.

  mirroring the established API-0030/API-0168 precedent of populating
  the `anyOf` branch with a realistic value to keep the wire body close
  to a realistic call.
- For numeric slots a pure string-suffix token (e.g.
  `mariadb-cov-save-external-port-0169-externalPort`) is not
  type-applicable. The convention established here for storyID
  traceability on numeric slots: pick a value that is BOTH semantically
  realistic (a valid TCP port in 1..65535 for a `*-saveExternalPort`
  field) AND embeds the storyID in its low digits — `25169` carries
  `0169` in the low digits while landing in the unprivileged port
  range. Future `*-saveExternalPort` operations on other tags
  (postgres/redis/mongo/mysql/etc.) should reuse the same
  `<25xxx>`-style integer-with-embedded-storyID scheme.
- Cardinality: API-0169 is structurally identical to API-0168 (two
  REQUIRED scalars, one plain string + one nullable scalar, no optional
  fields), but the second scalar's populated branch is
  `type: number` rather than `type: string`. The raw-API path is
  type-agnostic at the CLI level — the body is forwarded as opaque
  bytes — so the byte-for-byte body-comparison leg in
  `runAPICoverageSuccess` works identically for unquoted JSON numbers
  as for JSON strings.
- Insertion location: between API-0168 (mariadb-saveEnvironment) and
  the next-existing entry API-0188 (mounts-allNamedByApplicationId),
  not at file end — the `apiCoverageCases` slice is StoryID-sorted and
  the harness relies on that ordering for deterministic test names.
- Fixture token base `mariadb-cov-save-external-port-0169` follows the
  established `<tag>-cov-<slug>-<storyID>-<field>` suffix convention
  for git-grep traceability (slug derived from `saveExternalPort` →
  `save-external-port`, matching the kebab-case style established at
  API-0168 `mariadb-cov-save-environment-0168` for the analogous
  `*-save<Camel>` family).
- 401→CodeAuth harness-default failure leg retained; 404 override
  inapplicable (spec omits 404 — body-bearing imperative-action POST
  pattern), 400 not reserved here (payload validation is not the
  uniquely-distinguishing failure mode).
- Forward reference embedded for next entry: API-0170
  `mariadb-search` (GET). This will be the first GET on the mariadb/*
  roster since API-0164 `mariadb-one`, so the failure-leg override
  story may need re-evaluation (404→CodeNotFound is typically
  reactivated on by-id GETs).

  `environment-search` (6 params), and API-0296 `project-search`
  (5 params). The fixture pattern is now stable: populate exactly
  the four representative slices `q` (free-text), `projectId`
  (scoped filter), `limit` / `offset` (numeric pagination as decimal
  strings) regardless of how many extra optional params the spec
  declares — this keeps the diff narrow and the success-leg
  `r.URL.Query()` round-trip focused on the high-signal slots.

  `--input` JSON `query` field as canonical decimal strings (`"5"` /
  `"0"`); HTTP query strings are untyped on the wire so this is
  forward-compatible with a future schema validator that re-coerces
  to numbers.
- 404 declared on a `*-search` GET is structurally permissive — the
  harness-default 401→CodeAuth override is retained, and the 404
  override stays pinned to the canonical by-id GET (API-0164
  `mariadb-one` for this tag) per the cross-tag precedent. This
  discipline keeps a single, predictable failure mode per tag and
  avoids burning the 404 leg on operations where it is not the
  uniquely-distinguishing failure shape.

### Learnings for future iterations
- API-0138 establishes that the every-optional-populated rule
  (API-0010 / API-0014 / API-0249 / API-0292 / API-0297 / API-0052 /
  API-0053) is **conditionally overridden** when any optional field
  is OAuth credential-shaped. The two cases on the same gitea/* tag
  illustrate the rule cleanly:
    * API-0137 `gitea-testConnection`: optionals are `giteaId` +
      `organizationName` (no credential shape) → both populated per
      the every-optional-populated rule.
    * API-0138 `gitea-update`: optionals include `clientSecret` /
      `accessToken` / `refreshToken` (OAuth credential shape) →
      every optional omitted, fixture stays minimal-required-only.
  Future contributors landing a POST whose body has a mixed
  optional surface should default to the API-0131 `gitea-create`
  precedent: minimal-required-only when *any* optional is
  credential-shaped, even if the tag has prior every-optional-
  populated peers.
- The cross-tag update-by-id template is now triple-confirmed:
  API-0122 `domain-update`, API-0130 `environment-update`, and
  API-0138 `gitea-update` all share the spec shape "POST with no
  parameters, REQUIRED body, single/multiple required scalars
  identifying the resource, no 404 in the response set". When
  future *-update peers land (e.g. API-0144 `github-update`,
  API-0151 `gitlab-update`, API-0173 `mariadb-update`), the 404
  override is structurally inapplicable by precedent — the
  harness-default 401→CodeAuth failure leg is the right call.
- The gitea/* roster's required-arity profile across its eight
  operations: `gitea-create` (2 required), `gitea-getGiteaBranches`
  (2 required + 1 optional query), `gitea-getGiteaRepositories`
  (1 required + 1 optional query), `gitea-getGiteaUrl` (1 required
  query), `gitea-giteaProviders` (0 required, list endpoint),
  `gitea-one` (1 required query), `gitea-testConnection` (0
  required body + 2 optional), `gitea-update` (4 required body +
  11 optional). Closing the roster on the largest REQUIRED-arity
  body is incidental but useful: it leaves the contract surface
  fully exercised at every arity from 0..4.

  - Database-engine `*-create` operations are NOT byte-for-byte
    identical across the cluster. Relational engines (mariadb, mysql,
    postgres) carry a REQUIRED `databaseName` scalar that mongo omits
    because mongo creates databases lazily on first write. So the
    five-required-scalar mariadb-create cardinality is a relational-
    family default, NOT a database-tag default. Future contributors
    covering mongo-create/-update should expect the four-required-
    scalar shape; the equivalent mysql-create / postgres-create
    stories will likely revert to the five-required-scalar mariadb
    shape.

    `replicaSets` is mongo-specific; mariadb's `databaseRootPassword`
    is relational-specific). Each engine's create story carries a
    distinct optional surface and must re-verify the spec rather
    than copy a sibling fixture verbatim.
  - The minimal-required-only fixture rule (API-0131/API-0161) holds
    cleanly here: omitting all optionals keeps a single credential-
    shaped literal (`databasePassword`) in the fixture and protects
    the credential-redaction audit surface from drift.

  - The `apiCoverageCase` slice in `internal/cli/api_coverage_test.go` is indented with **1 tab** for case-element `{` / `},` and **2 tabs** for the field lines (StoryID/OperationID/etc.). Inside a `json.RawMessage(\`{ ... }\`)` literal, the **first** field after the opening `{` is at **2 tabs** (matching the SampleBody key indent — yes, this is unusual but is the established convention in the file) while subsequent fields are at **3 tabs**, and the closing `}\`),` returns to 2 tabs. The `Read` tool's tab visualization shows these as 3/3/4 tabs respectively because of how the harness expands tab characters; always cross-check with `od -c` before constructing an Edit anchor for this file.

Reuse the family choice (harness-default 401→CodeAuth) and the comment skeleton verbatim — the comment block's structural-identity callouts are load-bearing for future shape-positioning audits.
  - When inserting between two existing entries, use the boundary `\t\tSuccessResponse: \`{}\`,\n\t},\n\t{\n\t\tStoryID:     "<next-id>",` as the Edit anchor — it's 1-tab + 1-tab + 2-tab on the structural lines and is unique by next-StoryID. The `replace_all=false` Edit tool is unreliable when whitespace assumptions don't match; use a Python `str.replace` via `ctx_execute` for byte-accurate insertions when the anchor uses tabs.

- Results: 294/462 stories passing (63.6%).
- Remaining risks / follow-ups: none specific to this story. The next
  PRD-ordered priority-5 case is API-0142 `github-one` (declared GET
  per the spec preview). Per the slug-prefix-is-not-shape lesson, the
  next contributor must re-verify the spec at
  `internal/api/data/openapi.json > /github.one > get` before
  assuming the parameter axis or response set; the `*-one` slug
  historically takes a single REQUIRED `<tag>Id` query and is the
  canonical 404 → CodeNotFound failure-leg candidate, but neither
  fact is portable until the spec is re-read at the source.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **Zero-parameter GET pattern is a one-line struct.** When the
    spec declares zero parameters and no request body, the entry
    needs only `StoryID`, `OperationID`, `Method` (`http.MethodGet`),
    `Path`, `Tag`, and `SuccessResponse: '{}'` — every other field
    defaults correctly. `buildCoverageInputArgs` short-circuits and
    returns no extra args, so the CLI invocation is the terse
    `--json api call <op>` form with no `--input` flag at all. The
    `len(tc.SampleBody) > 0` content-type / body-byte comparison
    gate stays inert and the `range tc.SampleQuery` query-comparison
    loop iterates zero times. Reference peers: API-0058
    `certificates-all`, API-0376 `settings-isUserSubscribed`.
  - **No per-case fixture token when there are no payload fields to
    namespace.** Zero-parameter operations skip the
    `<tag>-cov-<slug>-<storyID>` fixture-token convention entirely
    because there is no request payload field to insert one into.
    This is codified at API-0376 `settings-isUserSubscribed` and now
    re-applied at API-0141.
  - **`*Providers` (collection-listing) slug stays parameter-free.**
    The bare `<tag>Providers` slug returns the account-wide
    collection of configured providers (e.g. every GitHub provider
    against the authenticated Dokploy account) rather than a
    specific provider keyed by id, so it pivots off the
    single-required-query shape used by `get<Tag>Branches` and
    `get<Tag>Repositories`. Useful prior-art when triaging
    `gitlabProviders`, `bitbucketProviders`, etc. — but the
    per-operation re-verification rule still applies.
  - **404 → CodeNotFound failure-leg override stays reserved for the
    by-id `*-one` peer.** The per-tag opener convention reasserted
    at API-0335..API-0444 and again here treats 404 → CodeNotFound
    as the canonical override for `*-one` resource probes only.
    Account-wide / platform-wide listings stick with the harness-
    default 401 → CodeAuth leg even when the spec declares 404.

  - **Cross-tag `*-search` shape is byte-for-byte identical across
    database tags**: mongo-search, mariadb-search, postgres-search,
    mysql-search, redis-search all declare the same eight optional
    query params (`q`, `name`, `appName`, `description`, `projectId`,
    `environmentId`, `limit`, `offset`). The API-0170 mariadb-search
    fixture is the canonical template; the next priority-4 `*-search`
    GETs (mysql/postgres/redis) should mirror it 1:1 with only the tag
    prefix and storyID swapped.

    `limit: "5"` / `offset: "0"` (not `"5.0"` / `"00"`) so a future
    schema validator that re-coerces query strings into the spec's
    `type: number` still accepts them. Stick to canonical decimal.

    one from each semantic axis (free-text, scoped filter, numeric
    pagination) rather than all eight — extra string filters of
    identical shape do not exercise any new code path on the round-
    trip and only inflate the diff.

    catch-all for spec-declared 404**: the family-choice rule
    re-asserted at API-0170 — and re-applied here — keeps 404 →

    resource is the dominant failure mode). A `*-search` GET's
    primary failure is unauthenticated access, not missing resource;
    401 → CodeAuth is the right representative-failure leg even when
    the spec lists 404 alongside 401.
  - **Slug-style lock-in (mongo/* preserves camelCase) is moot for
    single-segment slugs**: `mongo-cov-search-0184` is wire-equivalent
    in either convention; the kebab-vs-camel decision only matters for
    multi-segment slugs like `mongo-cov-saveExternalPort-0183` vs
    `mariadb-cov-save-external-port-0169`.
  - **`go test ./...` cache behaviour**: only `internal/cli`
    re-compiled / re-ran because that is the only package the patch
    touched. Sibling packages remained cached green. This pattern
    holds for every future API-coverage table addition.

    `<tag>Id` (string) scalar, 200 = `{}`, no 404 declared. When
    extending coverage to `postgres-remove` (API-0279) or
    `redis-remove` (likely a future priority-4 story), the new entry
    will be byte-for-byte cardinality-identical to API-0201
    `mysql-remove` modulo the resource-id field name; copy the
    fixture, swap `mysqlId` → `postgresId` / `redisId`, and renumber
    the `<tag>-cov-remove-XXXX` slug.

    `mysql-remove` share the *exact same* request body cardinality
    (single REQUIRED `mysqlId` scalar). The distinguishing assertions
    therefore derive entirely from the OperationID, Path, and StoryID
    scalars — the success/failure leg payloads are identical. Future
    entries that share a body shape with an existing peer should call
    out the equivalence in the comment block (as the API-0201 entry
    does) rather than tacit-copy-paste, so a future spec drift on
    either endpoint surfaces as an explicit comment-vs-fixture mismatch.
  - When inserting a new story into the StoryID-sorted slice, the most
    reliable Edit anchor is the previous entry's unique fixture literal
    (e.g. `"mysql-cov-reload-0200-appName"`) plus the closing `},` and
    the start of the next entry. Using only `SuccessResponse: \`{}\`,`
    + `},` + `{` is *not* unique because dozens of entries share that
    pattern.
  - The harness's representative-failure leg defaults to
    401→CodeAuth even when the spec declares 400 / 403 / 500. A 400
    or 404 override should only be elected when the operation's
    *uniquely distinguishing* failure mode is the override status code
    (e.g. API-0198 `mysql-one`, the canonical by-id GET, where the
    spec itself first declared 404 for the mysql/* roster). For every
    body-bearing imperative-action mysql POST whose spec omits 404,
    keep the 401→CodeAuth default — payload validation is not the
    operation's distinguishing failure mode.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The all-optional eight-parameter `*-search` GET family across
    the Dokploy database tags (mariadb / mongo / mysql / postgres /
    redis) shares the byte-for-byte identical parameter list:
    `q` (string), `name` (string), `appName` (string),
    `description` (string), `projectId` (string), `environmentId`
    (string), `limit` (number, default 20), `offset` (number,
    default 0). The cross-tag shape ancestor inside the covered
    roster is API-0170 `mariadb-search`; the most recent same-shape
    precedent is API-0184 `mongo-search`. New `*-search` entries
    on this 8-param shape should model their fixture and rationale
    block on API-0170 (and on API-0184 for any cross-database
    nuances like the 404→CodeNotFound override decision, which
    stays parked on the canonical `*-one` peer of each tag).
  - For all-optional `*-search` GETs, the established convention
    is to populate a representative subset of four params covering
    the three distinct semantic axes (free-text via `q`, scoped
    filter via `projectId`, paginated numerics via `limit` /
    `offset`) rather than all eight. Populating the remaining four
    optional string filters (`name`, `appName`, `description`,
    `environmentId`) is byte-for-byte redundant with `q` /
    `projectId` from the harness round-trip's perspective, so it
    only inflates the fixture without exercising any new code
    path. Numeric values use the canonical decimal grammar
    (`"5"` / `"0"`) so a future schema validator that re-coerces
    query strings to numbers still accepts them.
  - The 404→CodeNotFound failure-leg override is reserved for the
    canonical by-id `*-one` GET peer of each tag, NOT for the
    `*-search` GET. Even when the spec declares 404 on a `*-search`
    GET (as it does for mysql-search per the spec), the harness
    default 401→CodeAuth stays the most representative failure
    mode because search returns an empty result set on no-match,
    never 404. Sticking with the harness default also preserves
    the per-tag 401→CodeAuth invariant locked in by the kickoff
    operation (API-0194 `mysql-changeStatus` for the mysql/*
    roster).
  - The forward-reference comment at the END of the immediately
    prior entry remains the authoritative pointer to the next
    story — API-0203's tail block named API-0204 verbatim, which
    made the insertion location unambiguous. Always preserve and
    update this forward pointer; the new entry's tail must in
    turn name the next backlog story (API-0205 `mysql-start`
    here, a POST per the spec preview).

    `old_string` matcher is whitespace-sensitive — use `awk` /

    crafting an Edit.

  - **Empty-body POST cohort canonical pattern.** When an OpenAPI
    operation declares method POST with **no `requestBody` field at
    all** and **zero parameters**, the apiCoverageCase entry must
    leave `SampleBody`, `SampleQuery`, and `SamplePathParams` all
    nil. The harness's `len(tc.SampleBody) > 0` guard at
    `runAPICoverageSuccess` (line 31424) skips the Content-Type and
    body round-trip assertions; everything else (method, path,
    Authorization, schema_version, data.operation_id, data.method,
    data.status) is still asserted. API-0354
    `settings-cleanAllDeploymentQueue` was the first such case;
    API-0155 `licenseKey-deactivate` is the second. Future
    contributors hitting a no-body POST should grep for either entry.
  - **Spec re-verification is mandatory.** Even when the prior
    entry's forward-reference comment claims to know the shape (e.g.
    API-0154 said "the next contributor must re-verify the spec"),
    always read `internal/api/data/openapi.json` directly. Here the
    re-verification confirmed `licenseKey-deactivate` has *no*
    request body at all (degenerated from API-0154's
    single-required-string-scalar shape).
  - **Per-tag fixture-isolation namespace continuity.** A non-kickoff
    entry in a tag's roster inherits the namespace opened by the
    kickoff entry (here `licenseKey-cov-*` opened by API-0154). It
    must NOT back-reference any closed prior-tag namespace
    (`set-cov-*`, `gitProvider-cov-*`, etc.). The slug
    `licenseKey-cov-deactivate-0155` is reserved for `git grep`
    traceability even when no fixture literal is materialised on the
    wire (no body, no params).
  - **Failure-leg defaults.** Imperative-action POSTs without 404 in
    their response set retain the harness defaults (401 → CodeAuth
    via `tc.FailureStatus == 0` and `tc.FailureCode == ""`).
    400→CodeInvalidInput stays reserved for stories where payload
    validation is the operation's distinguishing failure mode; no
    payload to validate ⇒ no 400 representative is justified.

    new tag's roster (here postgres/*), the fastest way to derive
    the fixture shape is to grep prior `*-changeStatus` (or whichever
    operation is first in the StoryID-sorted backlog for the tag)
    entries. The mariadb/* (API-0160), mongo/* (API-0174), and
