    API-0272). The `<tag>-cov-<slug>-<storyID>` uniqueness rule is
    satisfied because slug and storyID differ across the two
    literals.
  - **StoryID-sorted slice with mixed priorities.** The
    `coveredAPIOperations` slice is StoryID-sorted, not
    priority-sorted. So when a priority-4 backlog story (API-0272)
    lands after a priority-3 story (API-0271 `port-update`), the new
    entry inserts immediately between them in the slice even though
    the priority-3 closing comment forward-references a *different*
    priority-3 story (API-0298 `redirects-create`). Both forward
    references are valid simultaneously because they refer to
    different orderings (priority-bucket order vs slice order).

  - **Five-required-string-scalar `*-create` cohort across the
    relational database tags.** `postgres-create` is the third
    member of a structurally identical cohort that also contains
    API-0161 `mariadb-create` and API-0195 `mysql-create`: same
    five REQUIRED slots (`name`, `environmentId`, `databaseName`,
    `databaseUser`, `databasePassword`), all plain non-nullable
    `type: string`. The non-relational sibling API-0175
    `mongo-create` is one slot narrower (no `databaseName`).

    mariadb/mysql expose. The minimal-required-only fixture rule
    historically defended against accidentally hard-coding two
    credential-shaped values in a single fixture (`databasePassword`
    + `databaseRootPassword`). For postgres-create that defensive
    posture is trivially satisfied because the second slot does not
    exist on the spec — but the rule is still applied uniformly
    so the redactor test family at
    `internal/cli/redaction_security_test.go` can extend coverage
    onto this case without re-deriving the literal.
  - **Cross-tag analog discovery for second-on-roster entries.**
    When a tag's coverage roster opens with a `*-changeStatus`
    case (here API-0272), the canonical second entry tends to be
    `*-create` (API-0273). The mariadb (API-0160 → API-0161),
    mongo (API-0174 → API-0175), and mysql (API-0194 → API-0195)
    rosters all follow the same alphabetic-by-operation pattern
    inside their priority-4 PRD window, so future contributors
    reaching a fresh `*-changeStatus` kickoff can pre-stage the
    `*-create` precedent search before opening the spec.
  - **StoryID-sorted slice with mixed priorities (re-confirmed).**
    The `coveredAPIOperations` slice stays StoryID-sorted, so the
    new API-0273 entry inserts immediately after API-0272 even
    though API-0290 `project-all` (priority 3) happens to sit at
    the next slot in the slice. Both forward references — priority-
    bucket order and slice order — remain valid simultaneously.

    set and `SampleBody` unset stay inert on the body / content-type code paths
    — no special-casing needed at the test-author level. The same is true for
    `r.URL.Query()` re-read on the success leg: it works uniformly across
    GETs whether the params are required (API-0276 `postgres-one`) or optional
    (this entry).
  - Per-tag fixture-isolation rule (originally established at API-0246
    `organization-active`, reasserted at API-0335..API-0444): any new entry
    on the postgres/* roster MUST stay inside the `postgres-cov-*` namespace
    and must NOT back-reference any closed prior-tag namespace literal. The
    cross-tag `*-search` precedent is referenced only structurally (same
    eight-param shape, same representative-subset choice, same
    family-choice rationale) — never via fixture-literal copy.

    **four** tags (`mariadb-start`, `mongo-start`, `mysql-start`,
    `postgres-start`) with byte-for-byte identical single-required-
    `<tag>Id`-string surfaces. Future contributors covering the next
    `*-start` peer (e.g. when a new database tag is introduced) should
    mirror the same single-field fixture and the same 401→CodeAuth
    family choice rather than re-deriving them — both are now de-facto
    invariants for the lifecycle-action `*-start` POST cluster.
  - **Tab-vs-space gotcha when editing api_coverage_test.go via Edit
    tool.** The Edit tool's `old_string` matching can be fooled by
    tab/space disagreement when the source is read into context with
    spaces but the on-disk file is tab-indented. If a normal Edit
    fails with "String to replace not found", drop into a Python
    `ctx_execute` snippet and write the file via raw-bytes
    `read → bytes.replace(anchor_bytes, replacement_bytes) → write`
    using literal `\t` characters in the anchor — the file uses
    `\t\t` (2 tabs) at the outer struct-element level and `\t\t\t`
    (3 tabs) at the field level. This is a recurring pattern when
    appending coverage entries to the very long
    `internal/cli/api_coverage_test.go` file.
  - The structural invariant "outer struct list elements use 2-tab
    indent, struct fields use 3-tab indent" is now confirmed via raw-
    bytes inspection at the API-0290 boundary; future contributors
    inserting between API-0283..API-0290 should preserve this so
    `gofmt` stays a no-op on the inserted block.

## 2026-05-09 - API-0303 - Cover redis-create (POST /redis.create)
- Implemented redis-create contract coverage. This is the second entry on
  the redis/* coverage roster, immediately following the API-0302
  redis-changeStatus kickoff and continuing inside the `redis-cov-*`
  per-tag fixture-isolation namespace. Completes the forward reference
  embedded in API-0302's closing block.
- Files changed:
  - internal/cli/api_coverage_test.go: added apiCoverageCase for
    redis-create inserted in StoryID order between API-0302
    redis-changeStatus and API-0331 security-create.
  - ralph/prd.json: flipped API-0303.passes to true.
  - ralph/progress.txt: this entry.
- Spec re-verified against `internal/api/data/openapi.json` >
  `/redis.create` > `post`: method POST, tag redis, no parameters,
  requestBody REQUIRED with application/json. **Three REQUIRED top-
  level fields** — `name` (string), `databasePassword` (string),
  `environmentId` (string). Four optional fields — `appName` (string),
  `dockerImage` (string, default `redis:8`), `description`
  (anyOf [string, null]), `serverId` (anyOf [string, null]). Responses
  200/400/401/403/500 with the 200 body `{}`
  (`additionalProperties: false`). **No 404** declared — mirroring
  every prior covered `*-create` mutation precedent (API-0118
  domain-create, API-0125 environment-create, API-0131 gitea-create,
  API-0161 mariadb-create, API-0175 mongo-create, API-0195
  mysql-create, API-0273 postgres-create, API-0298 redirects-create,
  API-0331 security-create).
- Shape positioning: three-required-string-scalar POST create-mutation
  with optional extension fields, body REQUIRED. **One narrower than
  the four-required-string-scalar API-0175 mongo-create precedent**
  (no `databaseUser`) and **two narrower than the
  five-required-string-scalar mariadb/mysql/postgres-create precedents**
  (no `databaseName`, no `databaseUser`). Redis is a single-instance
  KV store with no user authentication or pre-named database concept
  at create-time, which structurally explains the slimmer required
  projection.
- Family choice: harness-default 401→CodeAuth retained. Spec omits 404
  (404→CodeNotFound override structurally inapplicable to *-create
  mutations); 400→CodeInvalidInput is technically available but the
  harness reserves 400 representatives for stories where payload
  validation is the *uniquely distinguishing* failure mode. A
  conventional `*-create` mutation collapses to type-checking, so
  401→CodeAuth remains the most representative single failure mode,
  consistent with the redis/* kickoff at API-0302.
- Per the API-0131 / API-0161 / API-0175 minimal-required-only fixture
  rule (load-bearing for credential-redaction safety), the OPTIONAL
  configuration tail is **intentionally omitted** so a future
  credential-redaction audit cannot regress on a fixture that
  hard-codes any value beyond the REQUIRED `databasePassword` slot.
- Fixture token base `redis-cov-create-0303` follows the
  `<tag>-cov-<slug>-<storyID>` convention. The `databasePassword`
  literal carries the `<tag>-cov-<slug>-<storyID>-<field>` suffix
  for `git grep` traceability and so the redactor test family at
  `internal/cli/redaction_security_test.go` can extend coverage
  without re-deriving the literal. No collisions with API-0302's
  `redis-cov-changeStatus-0302` literals; full-tag-name slug `redis-`
  unambiguously distinct from `redirects-cov-*`.
- Verification run: gofmt -l . (clean), go mod tidy (clean), go vet
  ./... (clean), go test ./... (all green: internal/cli 1.454s),
  go test -race ./... (all green: internal/cli 3.192s).
  goimports/golangci-lint/staticcheck/govulncheck/goreleaser remain
  not installed locally; documented previously.
- Remaining risks or follow-ups: redis/* roster has nine more peers
  on the priority-4 backlog (API-0304..API-0312 redis-deploy through
  redis-update); each must continue inside the `redis-cov-*` namespace
  and re-verify the spec per the forward-reference lesson. Optional-
  field coverage (`appName`, `dockerImage`, `description`, `serverId`)
  for redis-create is deferred to a future story per the minimal-
  required-only rule.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The database-engine `*-create` family has a structural hierarchy:
    redis-create has 3 required strings (name, databasePassword,
    environmentId); mongo-create has 4 (adds databaseUser);
    mariadb/mysql/postgres-create have 5 (add databaseName).
    The differences map directly onto each engine's data model:
    redis is a single-instance KV store (no user, no named DB);
    mongo creates databases lazily on first write (no name) but
    requires a user; relational engines need both a user and a
    pre-named DB. This hierarchy also explains why redis-create
    can re-use the API-0175 mongo-create comment template wholesale
    — same family, narrower projection.
  - When opening a new tag's `*-create` peer (here: redis-create
    after the redis/* kickoff at API-0302 redis-changeStatus), the
    closest-peer to look up in the harness is the same-family
    `*-create` from a sibling database tag, not the same-tag
    kickoff: API-0302 redis-changeStatus is structurally a
    *-changeStatus (two-required-scalar status mutation) while
    API-0303 redis-create is structurally a *-create (three-or-more-
    required-string create mutation). Cross-tag family precedent
    beats same-tag opener precedent for shape inheritance, while
    same-tag opener precedent governs fixture-namespace isolation
    and family-choice (401→CodeAuth) consistency.
  - The minimal-required-only fixture rule (omit optional fields on
    `*-create` peers) is reasserted across every covered create
    mutation regardless of tag — its credential-redaction safety
    rationale applies uniformly because every database-engine
    create POST has a `databasePassword` field, and every config-
    type create POST has at least one fields-with-secrets adjacency
    risk. Future contributors adding redis-update / redis-saveX
    coverage should expect to reuse this rule verbatim.

  action move-mutation. **New shape inside the redis/* roster** —
  prior redis/* entries carried single-id POST (API-0302
  `redis-changeStatus`, API-0304 `redis-deploy`) or three-required-
  scalar create POST (API-0303 `redis-create`). The two-required-
  string-scalar move shape is the resource-relocation signature
  shared with every covered `*-move` peer (`<tag>Id` +
  `targetEnvironmentId`, both REQUIRED strings, no optional fields).
- **Family choice**: harness-default 401→CodeAuth retained. Spec
  omits 404 (404→CodeNotFound override structurally inapplicable to
  body-bearing imperative-action POST). 400→CodeInvalidInput is
  technically available but the harness reserves 400 representatives
  for stories where payload validation is the *uniquely
  distinguishing* failure mode. A move-mutation collapses to type-
  checking, so the harness-default 401→CodeAuth failure leg remains
  the most representative single failure mode, consistent with the
  401→CodeAuth choice locked in at API-0302..API-0304 across the
  redis/* arc.
- **Fixture token base** `redis-cov-move-0305` follows the
  `<tag>-cov-<slug>-<storyID>` convention. Verified non-colliding
  with API-0302's `redis-cov-changeStatus-0302`, API-0303's
  `redis-cov-create-0303`, and API-0304's `redis-cov-deploy-0304`
  literals (different slug + storyID → unique). Full-tag-name slug
  prefix `redis-` unambiguously distinct from lexically-adjacent
  `redirects-cov-*`.

  - `go mod tidy` — clean.
  - `go vet ./...` — clean.

  `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`, `govulncheck`, `goreleaser`.

    forward-references it; the next contributor must re-verify the

    forward-reference lesson before assuming any field shape.
- **Learnings for future iterations**:
  - The `*-move` family across all covered tags ships an *identical*
    two-required-string-scalar request body shape: `<tag>Id` +
    `targetEnvironmentId`, both REQUIRED strings, zero optional
    fields. application-move, compose-move, mariadb-move, mongo-move,

    name. Future `*-move` peers (none currently uncovered, but the
    pattern would generalize to any new `*.move` operation Dokploy

    swapping the field name and fixture token.

    request shapes: single-required-string-scalar (API-0302
    `redis-changeStatus`, API-0304 `redis-deploy`), three-required-
    string-scalar create (API-0303 `redis-create`), and two-required-

    representative regardless of body cardinality.
  - The spec's response set for `*-move` (200/400/401/403/500, no
    404) is consistent across every database-engine `*-move` peer

    `coveredAPIOperations` slice is StoryID-sorted by convention, and
    out-of-order priority backlogs are handled via the StoryID order
    (priority-5 API-0208 sits before priority-4 API-0246 because the
    sort key is the numeric StoryID, not the priority field).
  - The forward-reference comments at API-0157 `licenseKey-validate`
    accurately predicted API-0208 `notification-all` as the next
    priority-5 backlog entry. Trusting these forward-reference forecasts
    (after re-verifying the spec) saved a full PRD scan.
  - For parameter-free GETs (no parameters, no body, bearer-only auth),
    leaving every `Sample*` field unset is the explicit harness signal
    to skip fixture-file generation. The canonical agent invocation
    becomes `yalla api call <opId> --input '{}' --json` — note that the
    literal empty-object `--input` document is only required at the CLI
    layer, not at the harness level (the harness's `buildCoverageInputArgs`
    returns no flags when all `Sample*` fields are empty).
  - 404→CodeNotFound override is structurally inapplicable to
    parameter-free GETs even when the spec declares a 404 response,
    because there's no resource identifier the CLI could supply to
    surface a missing resource. The harness-default 401→CodeAuth leg
    therefore correctly captures the operation's representative failure
    mode.

  - The cross-tag `*-update` family across the database-service tags
    (mariadb / mongo / mysql / postgres / redis) is a direct one-to-
    one shape: a single REQUIRED top-level string scalar `<tag>Id`,
    a wide tail of 25–30 OPTIONAL fields (identity / credentials /
    runtime / resource limits / networking / applicationStatus enum /
    swarm-orchestration cluster / replicas / environmentId), and a
    `{}` 200 with `additionalProperties: false`, plus 200/400/401/403/
    500 (no 404). The body fixture is byte-equivalent across these
    five peers modulo the `<tag>Id` field name and the slug+storyID
    suffix. Future `*-update` POSTs in non-database tags must NOT
    assume this shape — the slug-prefix-is-not-shape lesson holds.
  - Within the redis/* roster, this entry is the fifth single-required-
    string-scalar POST peer (after API-0307 `redis-rebuild`, API-0309
    `redis-remove`, API-0313 `redis-start`, and API-0314 `redis-stop`).
    The body fixture is byte-equivalent across these five peers modulo
    the slug+storyID suffix. The redis/* roster's
    single-required-string-scalar micro-template chain ends here
    (every uncovered redis/* peer is now closed).
  - The redis/* roster's 404→CodeNotFound override remains pinned to
    API-0306 `redis-one`. The override was structurally inapplicable
    for every other redis/* peer because their specs omit 404 from
    the response set. This generalises across the database-service
    tags: each tag's 404 representative is the canonical by-id
    `*-one` GET, and body-bearing imperative-action POSTs / patch-
    style POSTs stay on the harness-default 401→CodeAuth invariant.
  - The redis-specific divergence from the postgres/mariadb/mongo/
    mysql `*-update` body is the absence of `databaseName` and
    `databaseUser` fields (only `databasePassword` survives) because
    redis is a single-keyspace key-value store rather than a multi-
    database server with named accounts. Future `redis-create` /
    `redis-update` schema-drift checks should re-confirm this
    divergence rather than assume cross-tag identity.

  - For closed all-required POSTs, the wire fixture must populate every
    declared property; the harness will not synthesise defaults for
    missing required keys and the success-leg invariant check exercises
    the body verbatim.
  - The kebab-case slug rule for the notification/* tag is now confirmed
    by two consecutive entries (API-0209 `create-custom`, API-0210
    `create-discord`); future peers MUST keep this style.
  - The `example.invalid` reserved-TLD URL convention is now a confirmed
    fixture pattern across the notification/* roster — anywhere the spec
    declares a URL-shaped string field (`endpoint`, `webhookUrl`,
    `serverUrl`, etc.), use `https://example.invalid/<namespace>-<field>`
    so a future URL-shape validator accepts it without risking real DNS
    lookups or wire egress.

    multi-camel notification/* roster) propagates cleanly: API-0211
    inherits `create-email` automatically from the per-tag-slug-style
    rule. Future siblings inherit kebab-case as well.

    action POSTs continue to hold (createCustom, createDiscord,
    createEmail, security-create, schedule-create, redirects-create,

- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - None for this story. Future volumeBackups/* peers (API-0446..
    API-0450) should grep this entry's slug-namespace banner to
    inherit the `volBackups-cov-*` namespace and the abbreviated
    `volBackups` fixture-prefix decision (see Learnings below).
  - API-0449 `volumeBackups-runManually` will be the first multi-
    camel-segment slug to land on the volumeBackups/* tag. Per the
    AGENTS.md per-tag-slug-style rule and the schedule/* precedent
    at API-0329 (camelCase suffix preservation,
    `schedule-cov-runManually-0329-*`), the recommended decision is
    camelCase preservation: `volBackups-cov-runManually-0449-*`.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **Abbreviated tag-prefix in fixture namespace.** This is the
    first per-tag namespace where the fixture prefix abbreviates the
    tag name: `volBackups-cov-*` (not `volumeBackups-cov-*`). The
    full `volumeBackups` tag name is preserved verbatim in the
    OperationID, Method, Path, and Tag fields of the apiCoverageCase
    literal — the abbreviation only affects the fixture string
    namespace. This decision keeps the SampleBody literal diff-
    friendly (each field key is suffixed with the per-field tag, so
    keeping the prefix short reduces line width). Future
    volumeBackups/* peers MUST inherit this `volBackups-cov-*`
    abbreviation. Future tags with similarly long names (e.g. any
    multi-word camelCase tag) may apply the same pattern, but the
    abbreviation choice is per-tag and must be locked at the
    kickoff entry (this one) and reasserted across the roster.
  - **The volumeBackups/* roster is structurally a near-mirror of
    the schedule/* roster.** Both expose the same operationId set
    (`*-create`, `*-delete`, `*-list`, `*-one`, `*-runManually`,
    `*-update`); both `*-create` declare the every-optional-
    populated optional tail; both `*-update` add an extra REQUIRED
    `*Id` slot to the create shape (the canonical *-update vs
    *-create delta locked at API-0330). However, the body schemas
    are NOT identical — volumeBackups-create has 5 required strings
    (vs. schedule-create's 3) and a different optional tail
    composition (anyOf-number-null `keepLatestCount`, anyOf-boolean-
    null `enabled`, plain boolean `turnOff`, multi-id slots for
    every Dokploy database type). Future contributors must re-verify
    against the spec rather than wholesale copying schedule/*
    fixtures.
  - **First five-required-string-scalar POST shape on the coverage
    table.** Promotes the API-0325 three-required-scalar shape and
    the API-0330 four-required-scalar shape. The progression
    suggests Dokploy's *-create endpoints scale REQUIRED string
    slots with the entity's identification surface (schedule
    requires only its scheduling fields; volumeBackups requires
    additionally the volume name, prefix, and destination).
  - **Multi-id-slot every-optional-populated tail.** The
    volumeBackups-create body declares seven distinct `*Id` slots
    (`applicationId`, `postgresId`, `mariadbId`, `mongoId`,
    `mysqlId`, `redisId`, `composeId`) — one per Dokploy service
    type the backup can target. The fixture populates ALL of them
    with deterministic strings, NOT just the one matching
    `serviceType: "application"`. Rationale: the every-optional-
    populated convention is byte-level (the harness asserts the
    body verbatim) and the schema does not enforce the
    serviceType↔id internal consistency at the type system level.
    A future server-side validator would likely reject a payload
    with seven populated id slots for a `serviceType: "application"`
    backup, but until that validator exists, the every-optional-
    populated rule wins. If a future spec revision adds
    `oneOf`-style discriminator constraints to the body schema,
    this fixture must be tightened to populate only the slot
    matching the chosen serviceType.

- **Remaining risks / follow-ups**:
  - The `botToken` slot embeds a per-bot Telegram secret in the request
    body. Like every prior body-borne secret in the notification/* roster
    (Discord/Lark/Slack/Teams `webhookUrl`, Email `password`, Ntfy
    `accessToken`, Pushover `userKey`+`apiToken`, Resend `apiKey`),
    this is a request-body field forwarded verbatim by yalla; the

    `*-create`. API-0219 closes the notification/* `create-*` cohort;
    API-0220 opens a new verb cohort and should grep the cross-tag
    parameter-free GET precedent (API-0006 `ai-getAll`, API-0098
    `deployment-allCentralized`, API-0246 `organization-active`)
    rather than the `create-*` chain.
- **Learnings for future iterations**:
  - `notification-createTelegram` is the **first eleven-slot
    four-string-seven-boolean pure-scalar closed-shape notification/*
    fixture**. No prior peer ships four REQUIRED string slots in a
    single create body, and no prior peer reaches eleven slots without
    either a number, an array, or a body-borne nested object. Previous
    eleven-slot peers — API-0212 `createGotify` (one number), API-0214
    `createNtfy` (one number + body-borne secret), API-0216
    `createResend` (one array-of-string) — all reached eleven via
    non-scalar slots. API-0219 reaches eleven purely by adding more
    string slots. Future `*-create` peers needing four or more
    REQUIRED string slots in a flat closed shape should grep this entry
    as the canonical reference.
  - Dokploy types Telegram `chatId` and `messageThreadId` as plain
    `string`, not as integers — even though Telegram itself returns
    these as 64-bit ints in its own API. The schema choice is
    deliberate: negative supergroup chat IDs (`-100xxxxxxxxxx`) and
    forum-topic IDs would otherwise risk JSON int-boundary precision
    loss. Always emit string values when populating these slots, and
    document the JSON-int-boundary rationale for any future peer that
    maps an upstream integer-ish ID into a string slot.
  - Telegram bot tokens follow the canonical `<bot_id>:<35-char-secret>`
    shape. The unallocatable all-zero bot-id leg (`0000000000:...`) is
    a safe sentinel — BotFather will never issue this prefix, so a
    leaked fixture cannot route to a real bot. Future peers shipping
    transport tokens with structured prefixes (e.g. AWS keys, GitHub
    PATs, Stripe keys) should hunt for analogous unallocatable-prefix
    sentinels rather than inventing arbitrary garbage strings — the
    structural shape preserves wire-format realism for downstream
    parsers while keeping the secret inert.
  - Per-spec rule reaffirmed once more: only the transport-agnostic
    core six booleans (`appBuildError`, `databaseBackup`,
    `volumeBackup`, `dokployRestart`, `appDeploy`, `dockerCleanup`)
    remain stable across notification/* siblings. Telegram keeps
    `serverThreshold` (joining Slack/Resend/Lark/Gotify/Pushover/Teams);
    Discord swaps it for `decoration`; Ntfy drops it entirely.
  - API-0219 closes the notification/* `create-*` cohort — every
    subsequent notification/* peer (API-0220 `getEmailProviders`,
    API-0221 `one`, API-0222 `receiveNotification`, API-0223
    `remove`, and the `test*` / `update*` family) belongs to a
    different verb cohort. The kebab-case slug-style rule fixed by the
    kickoff API-0209 `create-custom` is no longer in active extension
    inside this tag; new verb cohorts open their own slug anchors.

    has a target the caller can miss.

    rationale matches the cross-cohort discriminator rule — `null`
    is structurally identical to an omitted-key parse for a nullable
    field, so the on-wire fixture would lose the populated-vs-
    omitted distinction. Future peers (any tag) facing a nullable
    optional should grep this entry for the non-null-leg precedent
    and pick a documented spec-anchored literal (Pushover's `60` /
    `3600` here track the documented retry-floor and an in-bounds
    expire) rather than zero, the JSON default.
  - **Priority-value discriminator rule — provider scale anchors the
    fixture, "avoid JSON-zero default" is the invariant.** API-0227
    (Gotify, scale 0..10, midpoint 5) and API-0229 (Ntfy, scale
    1..5, midpoint 5) both pinned to their documented midpoints
    *and* to a non-zero non-default value. Pushover's scale (-2..2,
    default 0) cannot satisfy both rules at the documented midpoint
    (`0` is also the default). The discriminator rule wins:
    `priority: 1` (high priority) is the smallest non-zero non-
    boundary value that distinguishes the on-wire fixture from an
    omitted-key parse without crossing into the boundary value `2`
    ("emergency") whose validator path enforces `retry` / `expire`.
    Future cohort members with provider scales whose midpoint
    coincides with the JSON-zero default should pick the smallest
    spec-documented non-zero non-boundary value following this
    refinement.
  - **Boundary-value avoidance — uncoupling literal choice from
    optional-tail populated/null question.** Pushover's wire
    validator requires `retry` and `expire` to be present when
    `priority=2`. Pinning the REQUIRED `priority` to `2` would
    couple the priority literal choice to the optional-tail
    population question — the entry would then be unable to test
    optional-tail-omitted variants in any future companion test
    without cross-rewriting `priority`. Choosing `priority: 1`
    decouples the two concerns. Future entries with similar
    "validator-coupled-required-fields" boundary semantics
    (provider X, when `mode=Y`, requires fields A/B) should
    explicitly avoid the boundary REQUIRED literal so each
    optional-tail variant can be tested in isolation if needed.
  - **Cohort-opener forward reference list now extends through
    API-0229.** The API-0224 opener's comment names cohort peers by
    ID up through API-0234, and each subsequent member back-
    references the opener and prior members (this entry follows
    that discipline by naming API-0224 through API-0229 in its
    Slug-style and Shape-positioning blocks). The next cohort
    member API-0231 should append `API-0230 (→ test-pushover-
    connection)` to its Slug-style back-reference and update its
    Shape-positioning block to include the API-0230 three-required-
    plus-two-nullable-number positioning row.
  - **Indent-preserving PRD flip discipline still holds.** The
    `ralph/prd.json` file uses 2-space indent. We flipped
    `passes: false` → `passes: true` via a Python anchor-and-slice
    on the API-0230 story object so the diff stays a clean 1-line
    change; full file rewrite would risk re-indenting the entire
    462-story document.

    delta.** The Resend transactional-email API authenticates with
    a single bearer-style `apiKey` rather than the four-tuple SMTP
    credentials (`smtpServer`/`smtpPort`/`username`/`password`)

    fixture deliberately mirrors API-0226's `fromAddress` /
    `toAddresses` pair verbatim (single-entry array, deterministic
    `<local>@<host>.example.invalid` literals on the RFC 6761

    focused on the credential-tuple delta — replacing four SMTP
    fields with one bearer key. Future bearer-keyed transactional-
    email probes (e.g. SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark, if added to
    the spec) can mirror this entry without re-deriving the email-
    address shape conventions.

    sentinel for any email-shape fixture in this harness.** Both
    API-0226 (`smtpServer` + `from`/`toAddresses`) and API-0231
    (`from`/`toAddresses`) use it. Any future fixture carrying an
    SMTP host or email-shape literal should pick it up — never
    `example.com` (which has live MX records and would risk a real
    DNS lookup) or a TLD a future address-shape validator might
    reject.
  - **Three-required tuple has now been observed in three distinct
    optional-tail shapes.** API-0227 (three-required + one optional
    plain boolean), API-0230 (three-required + two optional
    nullable-number siblings), and API-0231 (three-required, zero
    optional). The cardinality-three-required invariant is the
    spine; the optional-tail variation is the structural delta.
    Future cohort entries that share the cardinality-three-required
    spine should explicitly note which prior peers they share the
    spine with and which optional-tail shape they carry, so the
    cross-entry diff stays focused on the optional-tail delta.
  - **Cohort opener forward-reference list now closes a member.**
    The API-0224 opener's forward-reference list named
    API-0231..API-0234 explicitly, so adding API-0231 here
    "closes" that forward reference for the eighth slot. Each
    subsequent member through API-0234 should continue to back-
    reference the opener and the prior members; once API-0234
    lands, the cohort is fully closed and the next notification/*
    story (API-0235 `notification-updateCustom`) opens a new shape
    family (mutation by-id, not connectivity-validation).
  - **Indent-preserving PRD flip discipline still holds via direct

  - REQUIRED `customId` (string) — persisted-notifier discriminator
    for the custom transport flavour; surfaces only on the
    `update*` cohort (create-mutations identify the row server-
    side).
  - OPTIONAL — every-optional-populated: `appBuildError`,
    `databaseBackup`, `volumeBackup`, `dokployRestart`, `appDeploy`,
    `dockerCleanup`, `serverThreshold` (booleans, all `true`),
    `name` (string), `endpoint` (https URL on `example.invalid`
    reserved TLD per RFC 6761), `headers` (single-entry
    `map[string]string`), and `organizationId` (string scope
    anchor). Mirrors the API-0209 fixture's optional tail one-for-
    one plus the additional `organizationId` scope anchor that
    surfaces only on the `update*` family (not on `create*`).
- Story count after this entry: 462 total, 409 passing, 53 still
  failing.
- **Remaining risks / follow-ups**: None for this story. The
  notification/* `update*` mutation-by-id cohort is now open with
  API-0235 as the kickoff member. The next pending notification/*
  story by priority is API-0236 `notification-updateDiscord`
  (priority=5), which should mirror this entry's two-required +
  every-optional-populated shape, swapping the optional tail for
  the matching `notification-createDiscord` (API-0210) sibling
  shape (Discord webhook URL + decoration flags) plus the
  required `notificationId`/`discordId` pair and the optional
  `organizationId` scope anchor.
- **Learnings for future iterations**:
  - **Cohort opener pattern.** When a story opens a new cohort
    (API-0235 opens the notification/* `update*` cohort after
    API-0234 closed the `test*` cohort), the opener's preamble
    should explicitly name the closed predecessor cohort, the
    new cohort's shape family, and the cross-tag update-by-id
    precedent list (API-0010, API-0050, API-0107, API-0122,
    API-0130, API-0193, API-0254). Cohort openers carry forward-
    reference lists naming the next 4-10 expected peers; this
    lets future iterations confirm cohort scope without re-
    deriving from the spec.
  - **Update-by-id divergence from the by-id-minimum precedent
    is intentional and tag-scoped.** API-0193 `mounts-update`
    establishes a by-id-minimum precedent (omit optional
    siblings to keep the minimal positive case shape-faithful).
    But the notification/* tag's house style for body-bearing
    mutations is every-optional-populated (locked at API-0209
    `notification-createCustom` and re-asserted at API-0050
    `backup-update`/API-0107 `destination-update`). The
    decision rule: **mirror the matching create-mutation
    sibling's optional-tail discipline rather than the cross-
    tag update-by-id minimum precedent**, since the per-tag
    create-precedent is closer in field-shape semantics. This
    rule should be applied to the rest of the notification/*
    `update*` cohort.
  - **`organizationId` scope anchor surfaces on `update*` but
    not `create*` family.** The spec for
    `notification-updateCustom` declares an optional
    `organizationId` field that is absent from
    `notification-createCustom`'s schema. The asymmetry exists
    because update mutations may need to re-scope a notifier
    from one organization to another (multi-tenant
    reassignment), while creates inherit the caller's
    organization scope server-side. Future notification/*
    `update*` peers should expect this `organizationId` slot in
    the spec and populate it in the fixture per the every-
    optional-populated convention.
  - **Two-required-string body cardinality (persisted-notifier
    flavour).** API-0235 introduces a new body cardinality on
    the notification/* tag — **two required scalars**
    (`notificationId` + transport-specific discriminator) — that
    every `update*` cohort peer is expected to re-assert,
    swapping the second discriminator for the transport-
    specific sibling row identifier (`discordId`, `emailId`,
    `gotifyId`, `larkId`, …). The cardinality is distinct from
    every prior notification/* peer: API-0208 (no body),
    API-0209 (two-required + eight-optional, no
    `notificationId`), API-0223 (single-required by-id), and
    the closed `test*` cohort (transport-descriptor bodies
    with no by-id target).
  - **PRD flip via regex anchor when JSON is large.** The
    `ralph/prd.json` file is ~1.7MB and 462 stories deep; the
    flip used a Python regex anchored on `"id": "API-0235"` to
    locate the story object then a substring slice on the
    trailing `"passes": false` to flip exactly one line. The
    2-space indent is preserved by the surgical slice — no
    full-file rewrite risk.

- **Verification run**:
  - `gofmt -w .` — clean.
  - `go mod tidy` — clean.
  - `go vet ./...` — clean.
  - `go test ./...` — all packages OK (`internal/cli` 1.351s,
    others cached).

    3.637s).
  - Optional tools (`goimports`, `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`,
    `govulncheck`, `goreleaser`) remain unavailable locally per
    the documented baseline; CI's `security` job covers them.
- **Remaining risks / follow-ups**:
  - API-0258 `patch-create` is the next patch/* peer (declared a
    POST per PRD with `requestBody.required = true`). It must
    continue inside the `patch-cov-*` namespace inherited from
    API-0256 and continued here, and re-verify the spec against
    `internal/api/data/openapi.json > /patch.create > post`
    before assuming any field shape, per the API-0345..API-0444
    forward-reference lesson.
  - The patch/* roster runs API-0256..API-0267 per `prd.json`
    (12 entries total, 2 now covered). Future contributors
    should grep this block first to inherit the `patch-cov-*`
    slug namespace rather than copying organization/* `org-cov-*`
    or port/* `port-cov-*` fixtures across the tag boundary.
- **Learnings for future iterations**:
  - **Required-outer-body + optional-inner-`serverId` is a
    cross-tag wire shape, not a per-tag idiom.** API-0387
    `settings-setupGPU` was the prior-tag exemplar and API-0257
    `patch-cleanPatchRepos` is the patch/* representative of the
    same wire shape. Both share: POST verb, zero parameters,
    `requestBody.required = true`, inner schema `{type: object,
    properties: {serverId: string}}` with no inner `required`
    array, response set 200/400/401/403/500 (no 404), 200 schema
    `{}` with `additionalProperties: false`. Future contributors
    encountering a Dokploy operation with this exact axis
    combination across any tag should grep both API-0387 and
    API-0257 for the populating-optional-`serverId` precedent
    rather than duplicating the rationale or leaving the body
    empty.
  - **`clean*` verb prefix is not authoritative for body shape
    even within the same tag.** The settings/* roster already
    established at API-0353..API-0359 that `clean*` siblings can
    diverge across the outer-body, inner-required, and parameter
    axes. The patch/* tag's only `clean*` peer (this entry,
    API-0257) sits squarely in the required-outer-body cohort,
    distinct from settings/* `cleanAll`/`cleanDockerBuilder`/
    `cleanDockerPrune` (optional-outer-body) and
    `cleanAllDeploymentQueue`/`cleanMonitoring`/`cleanRedis`/
    `cleanSSHPrivateKey` (no-body). Future patch/* `clean*`
    additions (none in the current PRD roster) must always
    re-verify per-operation rather than assume parity with this
    entry.
  - **Outer-body vs. inner-required axes are independent.** The
    `requestBody.required` flag controls whether the *body
    envelope* is mandatory; the inner schema's `required` array
    controls whether *individual fields* are mandatory. API-0257
    has `requestBody.required = true` (the body envelope must be
    sent) but the inner schema has no `required` array (every
    field is optional, including `serverId`). This means the
    minimum-valid wire payload is `{}`, but the request line
    must still carry a Content-Type header and a body. Future
    contributors authoring required-body fixtures should always
    populate at least one optional field (per the API-0353 /
    API-0387 precedent) so the body-forwarding round-trip
    assertion remains meaningful.

- Failure leg: harness-default 401→CodeAuth retained. The spec
  omits 404 (POST-style toggle on this Dokploy surface emits 400
  for an unknown `patchId` rather than 404 — the by-id GETs at
  API-0256/API-0262/API-0263/API-0264 carry 404 only because they
  are *lookups*, not mutations), so the 404→CodeNotFound
  override is structurally inapplicable. 400→CodeInvalidInput is
  technically available but the harness reserves 400
  representatives for stories where payload validation is the
  uniquely distinguishing failure mode; the success-leg fixture
  here always carries both required scalars with structurally
  valid types, so the validator surface is not exercised on the
  failure leg. Auth remains the universal failure mode every
  authenticated Dokploy operation must re-prove.
- Fixture token base: `patch-cov-toggle-enabled-0266`. Verified
  unique against every prior `patch-cov-*` token (API-0256
  `patch-cov-by-entity-id-0256`, API-0257
  `patch-cov-cleanPatchRepos-0257`, API-0258
  `patch-cov-create-0258`, API-0259 `patch-cov-delete-0259`,
  API-0260 `patch-cov-ensure-repo-0260`, API-0261
  `patch-cov-mark-file-for-deletion-0261`, API-0262
  `patch-cov-one-0262`, API-0263
  `patch-cov-read-repo-directories-0263`, API-0264
  `patch-cov-read-repo-file-0264`, API-0265
  `patch-cov-save-file-as-patch-0265`) and orthogonal to every
  prior tag's `*-cov-*` namespace.
- Files changed:
  - `internal/cli/api_coverage_test.go` (+1 case, ~178 lines
    including rationale comments).
  - `ralph/prd.json` (`API-0266.passes = true`).
  - `ralph/progress.txt` (this entry).
- Verification run:
  - `gofmt -w .` — clean (`gofmt -l .` reports no diff).
  - `go mod tidy` — clean (no new deps).
  - `go vet ./...` — clean.
  - `go test ./...` — all packages OK (`internal/cli` 1.534s).
  - `go test -race ./...` — all packages OK (`internal/cli`
    3.406s).
  - `go build ./...` — clean.
  - `goimports`, `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`, `govulncheck`,
    `goreleaser` not installed locally; skipped per the
    document-rather-than-silently-skip rule.
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - 32 priority-5 API stories still pending; next in PRD order
    is API-0267 `patch-update` (POST per spec preview) which
    closes the patch/* roster. The next contributor must
    re-verify the spec against
    `internal/api/data/openapi.json > /patch.update > post`
    before assuming any field shape (the spec preview shows a
    seven-field surface with single-required `patchId` plus six
    optional fields including a `{create, update, delete}`
    enum, two booleans/strings, and a nullable `updatedAt`),
    and continue inside the `patch-cov-*` per-tag
    fixture-isolation namespace until the patch/* roster
    closes.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **Required-boolean POST body is a new wire-shape leg in
    the patch/* roster.** API-0258 `patch-create` already
    carries an `enabled` boolean but as an *optional* field,
    so the success-leg fixture there can omit it without
    affecting structural validity. Here `enabled` is required,
    so the wire payload must always include it; we picked
    `true` to match the natural enable-toggle direction
    implied by the operation name. A future contract-test
    extension that exercises both boolean legs (`true` and
    `false` explicitly) should add a sibling case rather than
    mutating this one — same rule we used at API-0265 for the
    optional `patchType` enum.
  - **No-optional-surface POST bodies skip the
    every-optional-populated expansion entirely.** When the
    schema declares zero optional fields the canonical
    "minimum-required-fields" payload that
    `runAPICoverageSuccess` validates is identical to the
    maximally-populated payload, so there is no expansion
    decision to document — in contrast to API-0265
    `patch-saveFileAsPatch` (deliberate omission of the
    optional `patchType` discriminator) or API-0258
    `patch-create` (optional discriminator / boolean /
    nullable-id fan-out).
  - **Mutating-POST cohort response set canonical at
    200/400/401/403/500.** Every patch/* mutation covered to
    date (API-0257/0258/0259/0260/0261/0265/0266) carries the
    same response set with no 404 — Dokploy POSTs that mutate
    state route unknown-target errors through 400, not 404.
    The 404-bearing shape is reserved for the by-id GET cohort
    (API-0256/0262/0263/0264). Future patch/* contributors
    should keep the 401→CodeAuth harness-default representative
    for both shapes unless a story has a *uniquely
    distinguishing* validator surface that justifies a 400 leg.
  - **Per-tag fixture-token uniqueness audit must enumerate
    every prior entry in the `patch-cov-*` namespace, not just
    the most recent.** The roster now has ten prior fixture
    tokens; future contributors must grep the entire namespace
    before picking a slug to avoid silent collision in subtest
    names that run in parallel via `t.Parallel`.

  - The 404 → CodeNotFound override at the by-id `*-one` peer is the
    canonical home for the resource-not-found failure mode under
    Dokploy's tRPC convention, and the per-tag opener (here API-0316
    `registry-all`) explicitly reserves it for the `*-one` peer. Mark
    this clearly in the override's design-rationale block so a future

    counts and verify the cross-tag chain stays linear.

    rather than SampleBody for `*-one` style readers. The harness's

    the per-tag deterministic-but-clearly-fake naming convention; the

    (API-0136, API-0164, API-0178, API-0198, API-0276, API-0306).
  - `runAPICoverageFailure` reads `tc.FailureStatus` and
    `tc.FailureCode` and falls back to 401 / `yerr.CodeAuth` when
    either is zero — opting in to the override is just a two-field
    struct addition, no harness change needed.
